articles.headline: Opposition marches against CEC in display of force at Ramlila Maidan
articles.summary: Leaders of the INDIA bloc, including Rahul Gandhi and Akhilesh Yadav, held a massive 'Chalo Dilli' protest against the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. They accused the Election Commission of deleting voters at the BJP's behest. Over 50,000 supporters attended the rally, which leaders called a battle to 'save democracy' ahead of upcoming state and 2027 assembly elections.

articles.headline: GST collections surge 23% to ₹2.31 lakh crore in October
articles.summary: India's gross GST revenue rose 22.9% year-on-year to reach ₹2,31,290 crore in October 2026, marking the second-highest monthly collection since the tax regime's 2017 launch. The growth was driven by strong domestic transactions and a 42.2% jump in import-linked revenue. Experts attribute the surge to robust festival demand and improved compliance measures across sectors.

articles.headline: Cyclone Murasu forms over Bay of Bengal, landfall expected tomorrow
articles.summary: A deep depression over the Bay of Bengal has intensified into cyclonic storm 'Murasu,' moving toward the southern Odisha and northern Andhra Pradesh coasts. With wind speeds expected to reach 120kmph, the IMD has issued a severe weather warning. Odisha and Tamil Nadu are on high alert, with rescue teams deployed and residents in low-lying areas being evacuated.

articles.headline: LCA Mk-1A stealth fighter central to IAF's modernization vision
articles.summary: IAF Chief Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit identified the Tejas LCA Mk-1A as the top priority for the force's modernization. The aircraft is expected to enter service shortly, with plans to also integrate the LCA Mk-2 and Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA). The chief emphasized self-reliance (atmanirbharta) in weaponry and sensors to meet operational demands and deter conflict.

articles.headline: Trump prepares to wield executive power if Democrats win US Congress
articles.summary: Advisors to Donald Trump are reportedly drafting plans to bypass legislative gridlock through executive actions if Democrats take control of the US Congress. The strategies focus on immigration, tariffs, and reallocating federal funds. Trump suggested he would be 'Mr. Veto' to block Democratic legislation while using the federal bureaucracy to enact his policy agenda aggressively.

articles.headline: Air quality takes a nosedive in Delhi as curbs kick in
articles.summary: Delhi's air quality deteriorated to the 'very poor' category with an AQI of 261, leading to the enforcement of pollution-control measures. Authorities have banned non-essential construction and demolition activities. Additionally, over 7,200 vehicles were checked at borders, with 714 non-BS-VI compliant vehicles turned back as stubble burning contributions rose to 18.57%.

articles.headline: SC to hear first batch of Noida Sports City petitions in December
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has scheduled the first hearing for pending Sports City projects in Noida for December 9. The court will address challenges by home buyers and developers against the Noida Authority's decision to stall projects in Sectors 78, 79, and 150. The legal battle centers on allegations of master plan violations and the non-delivery of promised sports infrastructure.

articles.headline: Delhi LG calls on students to join efforts to clean Yamuna
articles.summary: Lieutenant Governor VK Saxena urged students from Delhi Public Schools to participate in 'Ganga-Ek Aviral Dhara' to help rejuvenate the Yamuna River. Speaking at a cleaning drive, the LG noted that the Yamuna accounts for 76% of Delhi's pollution despite the city having only 2% of the river's total length. He emphasized youth involvement in preserving India's civilizational history.

articles.headline: India's crude oil imports surge to a record high in October
articles.summary: Crude oil imports rose to roughly 5.6 million barrels per day in October as refiners maximized purchases from Russia and the Middle East ahead of winter. Russian shipments remained dominant despite shipping risks in the Red Sea. The surge reflects India's growing domestic fuel demand and refiners' efforts to secure lower-cost supplies amidst global geopolitical volatility.

articles.headline: Trump talks to Netanyahu as US mulls new strikes on Iran
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump spoke with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu regarding potential new military action against Iran following recent missile exchanges. The call comes as the US maintains a high-intensity naval presence in the region. Reports suggest the US is considering targeting up to eight locations in Iran to deter further aggression against Israel and US assets.

articles.headline: CBSE collected ₹16.47 crore from students for post-result result verification
articles.summary: RTI data reveals that the CBSE collected over ₹16 crore from Class 12 students seeking marks verification, re-evaluation, and answer sheet copies in 2026. While the board promised full refunds if marks increased, many students reported they did not receive payments. The data also showed that a significant percentage of re-evaluation requests resulted in no change to original scores.

articles.headline: Bengal CM promises citizenship to 2.5 lakh Bangladeshi Hindu refugees
articles.summary: West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee announced that 250,000 members of the Dalit Matua community, who migrated from Bangladesh, will be issued citizenship certificates by the state. The move follows years of political debate over refugee status in the state. Banerjee stated the enrollment process would begin in January 2027 to ensure permanent residency and voting rights.

articles.headline: Indian stock markets hit all-time highs following RBI dividend announcement
articles.summary: The BSE Sensex and NSE Nifty 50 reached record high levels as investors cheered the Reserve Bank of India's unprecedented dividend transfer. The financial boost is expected to improve government finances and banking sector liquidity. Major gainers included state-run banks and heavyweights, contributing to a significant surge in overall market capitalization during the afternoon trade session.

articles.headline: Political parties shift focus to Phase 6 polling in Lok Sabha elections
articles.summary: Campaigning has intensified for the sixth phase of the Lok Sabha elections, covering 58 constituencies across six states and two Union Territories. Top leaders from the BJP and the INDIA bloc are holding multiple rallies to sway voters. Key issues discussed include economic growth, unemployment, and constitutional protections as the marathon election process enters its final stages.

articles.headline: IMF upgrades India’s growth forecast citing strong domestic demand and investment
articles.summary: The International Monetary Fund has revised India's GDP growth forecast upward, highlighting the country's resilience amidst global economic uncertainty. The IMF pointed to strong private consumption and public investment as primary drivers of growth. However, the report also warned about the need for continued structural reforms to sustain this momentum and manage inflation effectively.

articles.headline: Severe heatwave persists in North India with temperatures exceeding 45 degrees
articles.summary: Intense heatwave conditions are sweeping across Northern and Central India, with several cities recording temperatures above 45 degrees Celsius. The weather department has issued red alerts for Rajasthan, Punjab, and Haryana. The extreme heat has led to a surge in power consumption, testing the national grid's capacity as demand for cooling appliances hits peak levels across the region.

articles.headline: Home Minister Amit Shah addresses major campaign rallies in Bengal and Odisha
articles.summary: Home Minister Amit Shah held multiple campaign rallies in West Bengal and Odisha, attacking the opposition over regional issues and development. He emphasized the government's commitment to national security and economic progress. The rallies are part of the BJP's push to expand its footprint in eastern India during the critical final phases of the ongoing Lok Sabha elections.

articles.headline: Air India Express restores normal operations after recent cabin crew disruptions
articles.summary: Air India Express has successfully restored its full flight schedule following a period of cancellations caused by a localized cabin crew strike. The management has resolved major issues with the crew union regarding HR policies and staff integration following the merger process. The airline is now focusing on improving on-time performance and passenger communication systems.

articles.headline: NHAI accelerates construction of fifteen key expressway projects for current fiscal year
articles.summary: The National Highways Authority of India has announced plans to accelerate the completion of 15 key expressway projects within the current fiscal year. The move aims to improve regional connectivity and logistics efficiency. Significant budgetary allocations have been earmarked for the Delhi-Mumbai and Bengaluru-Chennai corridors to ensure timely project delivery and quality standards.

articles.headline: Nvidia results awaited as litmus test for global AI technology rally
articles.summary: Global markets are on edge ahead of Nvidia’s quarterly earnings report, which is seen as a key indicator for the artificial intelligence boom. Analysts expect massive revenue growth from the chipmaker. The results are likely to set the tone for technology stocks globally, including Indian IT firms, which have been increasingly integrating AI services into their service portfolios.

articles.headline: International Criminal Court seeks arrest warrants for leaders in Gaza conflict
articles.summary: The International Criminal Court is seeking arrest warrants for senior leaders for alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity. The prosecutor cited evidence of intentional targeting of civilians and starvation as a weapon of war. This move has drawn significant international reactions, with some nations supporting the judicial process and others criticizing the timing and jurisdiction.

articles.headline: Kolkata Knight Riders secure spot in IPL final after dominant playoff win
articles.summary: The Kolkata Knight Riders have advanced to the final of the Indian Premier League 2024 after a convincing victory in the first qualifier. The team’s bowling unit put up a stellar performance, restricting the opposition to a low total. This victory makes KKR the first team to secure a place in the championship match, demonstrating their consistent form throughout the entire tournament.

articles.headline: Calcutta High Court Cancels All OBC Certificates Issued After 2010
articles.summary: The Calcutta High Court struck down the OBC status of 77 classes, primarily Muslim groups, granted in West Bengal since 2010. The court found the reservations unconstitutional and not based on proper data regarding social backwardness. Around five lakh certificates are expected to be affected, though those who already obtained jobs or benefits will not be displaced.

articles.headline: PM Modi Expresses Confidence in Securing Majority in General Elections
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi stated in an interview that he is certain the NDA will surpass its previous tallies in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. He emphasized that the results on June 4 would set a new record for the coalition. Modi dismissed opposition claims and focused on his government's track record of development and global standing over the last decade.

articles.headline: IMD Issues Red Alert as Severe Heatwave Grips Northern India
articles.summary: The India Meteorological Department issued a red alert for several states, including Delhi, Punjab, and Rajasthan, due to severe heatwave conditions. Temperatures crossed 47 degrees Celsius in multiple locations. The department advised citizens to avoid sun exposure during peak hours, as hot and dry winds are expected to continue for the next few days.

articles.headline: Bibhav Kumar Remanded to Judicial Custody in Swati Maliwal Assault Case
articles.summary: A Delhi court sent Bibhav Kumar, the personal aide to CM Arvind Kejriwal, to judicial custody. Kumar is accused of assaulting AAP MP Swati Maliwal at the Chief Minister's residence. The police are currently examining forensic data from Kumar's phone and CCTV footage from the premises to corroborate the victim's statement and establish the sequence of events.

articles.headline: Government Releases New Guidelines to Standardize School Bag Weights
articles.summary: The Ministry of Education issued a revised School Bag Policy to reduce the physical burden on students. The guidelines mandate that the weight of school bags should not exceed 10% of a student's body weight. It also suggests that schools should provide digital lockers and ensure that textbooks are developed in a lightweight format to prevent spinal issues.

articles.headline: Pune Porsche Crash: Police Investigate Possible Evidence Tampering by Doctors
articles.summary: Investigations into the Pune Porsche crash involving a minor have shifted toward potential tampering with blood samples at Sasoon Hospital. Authorities suspect that the original samples were replaced to show no alcohol consumption. The minor’s father and grandfather are in custody as the probe widens into how the family allegedly influenced the initial police response.

articles.headline: NHAI Postpones Annual Toll Hike Across National Highways Until June
articles.summary: The National Highways Authority of India decided to defer the annual increase in toll rates until after the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. The hike, which typically ranges between 5% and 10% based on inflation, was originally scheduled for April. This move aims to avoid placing additional financial burdens on commuters during the ongoing polling season.

articles.headline: India to Send Official Delegation to Iran for President Raisi's Funeral
articles.summary: Vice President Jagdeep Dhankhar will represent India at the official funeral ceremony of Iranian President Ebrahim Raisi in Tehran. India observed a day of national mourning following the helicopter crash that killed the President and Foreign Minister. The visit underscores the strategic partnership between the two nations, particularly regarding regional connectivity.

articles.headline: ISRO Begins Testing of 3D-Printed Liquid Rocket Engine for Future Missions
articles.summary: The Indian Space Research Organisation successfully conducted a hot fire test of a 3D-printed liquid rocket engine. The engine, developed for the PSLV upper stage, reduces the number of parts from 14 to 1. This innovation is expected to significantly cut production time and costs for future satellite launch vehicles and deep space exploration missions.

articles.headline: Health Ministry Issues Advisory on Rising Cases of Seasonal Flu
articles.summary: The Union Health Ministry issued a national advisory regarding a surge in seasonal influenza cases across several states. The document outlines protocols for early screening and treatment to prevent complications in high-risk groups like the elderly and children. Officials emphasized that while the strain is not highly virulent, masking in crowded areas is recommended.

articles.headline: Government Plans Launch of AI-Powered Portal for Farmers
articles.summary: The Ministry of Agriculture is set to launch a new platform that utilizes artificial intelligence to provide real-time crop advice to farmers. The portal will integrate weather data, soil health reports, and market prices to help producers make informed decisions. It is designed to operate in multiple regional languages to ensure accessibility for rural communities.

articles.headline: Norway, Spain, and Ireland Announce Formal Recognition of Palestinian State
articles.summary: In a landmark move, Norway, Ireland, and Spain officially announced their recognition of a Palestinian state to rejuvenate the two-state solution. Israel responded by immediately recalling its ambassadors from the three countries, calling the move a distorted step. The decision reflects growing European pressure for a diplomatic resolution to the ongoing conflict.

articles.headline: ASI Completes Conservation Work on Ancient Sun Temple Sculptures
articles.summary: The Archaeological Survey of India announced the completion of its latest restoration phase at the Konark Sun Temple. The project focused on chemical cleaning and structural strengthening of external sculptures affected by salt air. Experts used specialized mortars to fill cracks while ensuring the preservation of the intricate 13th-century stone carvings.

articles.headline: KKR Dominates SRH to Secure Spot in IPL 2024 Final
articles.summary: Kolkata Knight Riders reached their fourth IPL final after an eight-wicket victory over Sunrisers Hyderabad in Qualifier 1. Mitchell Starc’s early three-wicket burst dismantled the SRH top order, restricting them to 159. Venkatesh Iyer and Shreyas Iyer then struck unbeaten half-centuries to chase down the target in just 13.4 overs at Ahmedabad.

articles.headline: Retail e-invoicing pilot likely from April 2027
articles.summary: GST authorities plan a pilot project from April 1, 2027, to electronically record retail invoices in select sectors. This aims to improve tax compliance by helping officials verify sales reporting and GST payments, building on existing business-to-business e-invoicing.

articles.headline: Telcos seek higher int’l call termination charges
articles.summary: Indian telecom providers have requested the sector regulator, Trai, to increase international termination charges (ITC) to at least ₹5 per minute from the current 65 paise. This push aims for global parity amid rupee depreciation, as ITC is settled in US dollars, impacting telcos' realisations.

articles.headline: RBI’s net short dollar forward position hit record $239 bn in Sep
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India's outstanding net short dollar position in the forward market reached a record $239.2 billion by September end, up from $200.06 billion in August. This surge was influenced by a special swap window for banks to mobilize foreign currency non-resident deposits.

articles.headline: Cyberattacks push up insurance claims
articles.summary: Insurance claims from cyberattacks on banks and businesses have surged, exceeding ₹150 crore for banks alone in H1 FY27. Despite the rise in losses from data breaches and ransomware, premiums remain soft due to abundant reinsurance capacity and new market entrants.

articles.headline: When gold loses its glitter
articles.summary: A regulatory framework effective April 2026 aims to mitigate risks in gold loans, but more action is needed. Gold loan portfolios have rapidly expanded, driven by rising gold prices, increased risk weights on unsecured credit, and new regulatory adjustments that lifted loan-to-value ceilings for small loans.

articles.headline: Last-mile banking network is struggling
articles.summary: India's last-mile banking network, relying on 1.2 million business correspondents (BCs), is struggling due to low and unsustainable commissions, volatile footfall, and high attrition. Despite its crucial role in financial inclusion, the average monthly payout for BCs has declined, impacting their long-term participation and the network's viability.

articles.headline: BoB to reinvest MDR proceeds into UPI ecosystem: MD & CEO
articles.summary: Bank of Baroda (BoB) MD & CEO Debadatta Chand announced the bank will reinvest Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) proceeds from select UPI transactions into improving UPI technology and infrastructure, rather than using it for profit. This aims to enhance services and sustainability of the digital payments ecosystem.

articles.headline: India’s R&D well placed to lead global mfg, AI: Rockwell CFO
articles.summary: Rockwell Automation CFO Christian Rothe states India is strategically positioned to leverage its R&D expertise in advanced manufacturing, automation, and AI. With nearly 20% of Rockwell's global headcount in India and over 50% being engineering talent, India significantly contributes to the company’s global technology development.

articles.headline: More women at work in India, but on worse terms: Icrier study
articles.summary: A new Icrier study reveals India's women workforce nearly doubled in seven years to 201 million, but growth was concentrated in agriculture, self-employment, and unpaid family work. Women face shorter hours and a widening pay gap, with nominal monthly wages growing 41% for rural women vs 65% for rural men since 2017-18.

articles.headline: Companies pessimistic about economy, bullish on business
articles.summary: IMA India's Q3 FY27 Business Confidence and Performance Index shows business leaders are increasingly anxious about the economy (index fell to 45.7, below neutral 50) but more confident about their own businesses (business sentiment index rose to 62.1). This divergence is unprecedented, driven by macroeconomic concerns vs strong profitability and capex expectations.

articles.headline: Net GST collection grew 25.6% in Oct, fastest in FY27
articles.summary: India's net GST collection surged 25.6% year-on-year to ₹2.03 trillion in October, marking the fastest growth rate this fiscal year. Gross GST mop-up also grew 22.9% to ₹2.31 trillion. Import-linked GST significantly outpaced domestic collection, rising 42.2% from imports.

articles.headline: PV wholesales rose 12.4% in Oct on festive demand
articles.summary: Domestic wholesales of passenger vehicles increased 12.4% year-on-year to 528,384 units in October. This growth was spurred by strong festive demand, last year's GST rate cuts, income-tax relief, and lower interest rates, enhancing vehicle affordability and encouraging upgrades.

articles.headline: InGovern: Valuation change alone no grounds to reopen family settlement
articles.summary: Corporate governance advisory firm InGovern Research Services stated that a documented family arrangement should not be reopened solely due to business valuation changes, citing the ongoing TVS group succession dispute. Any reinterpretation must align with agreement terms and law, without disrupting listed company operations.

articles.headline: SFIO gets NCLT nod to recover ~5.4K cr from Bhushan Power
articles.summary: The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT), New Delhi, allowed the Serious Fraud Investigation Office (SFIO) to recover approximately ₹5,431 crore allegedly siphoned from Bhushan Power & Steel Ltd (BPSL). The NCLT rejected challenges from former promoters, citing Section 32A of the IBC, emphasizing that resolution plans do not end fraud allegations.

articles.headline: Indian mkt matured for bespoke luxury cars: JLR India MD
articles.summary: Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) India MD Rajan Amba stated that India has matured into a market for bespoke luxury vehicles, with customers increasingly appreciating exclusive offerings. JLR has seen success, evidenced by 15 of 18 limited-edition Range Rover SV Sawai Collection vehicles being pre-booked.

articles.headline: GST Council’s decriminalisation move a significant reform: CII
articles.summary: The Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) lauded the GST Council's decisions on decriminalization and enforcement rationalization as significant institutional reforms. CII views these measures, including the proposed removal of arrest powers under Section 69 of the CGST Act, as a landmark shift towards trust-based economic governance.

articles.headline: Bosch arm eyes double-digit share in India AC market
articles.summary: Bosch Home Comfort Group, launching Bosch-branded air conditioners next year, aims for a double-digit market share within two years. The European heating and cooling solutions provider plans to invest around ₹900 crore over the coming years to secure a top-five brand position in the medium term.

articles.headline: Cordelia aims to bring India among top 5 mkts
articles.summary: Cordelia Cruises aims to position India among the top five global cruise markets by 2032. The company plans fleet expansion, including Cordelia Sun, to tap into the growing domestic cruise tourism potential, currently operating two ships, Empress and Sky.

articles.headline: CCI approves Prosus proposal to buy stake in Sachin Bansal’s Navi
articles.summary: India's competition watchdog, CCI, approved Dutch investment group Prosus's acquisition of a stake in Sachin Bansal-led fintech firm Navi. This move allows Prosus to expand its presence in India’s digital financial services sector, with its MIH Payments Holdings BV holding investments in various portfolio companies operating in India.

articles.headline: Syngene expects stronger H2FY27 on order book
articles.summary: Syngene International anticipates improved revenue in H2 FY27, driven by its order book and customer delivery commitments, maintaining its full-year guidance of a single-digit revenue decline. Q2 FY27 revenue rose 13% sequentially to ₹833 crore, aided by contract development and manufacturing, but was down 9% year-on-year.

articles.headline: Annual investments may go above ~500-600 cr: Sona Comstar MD
articles.summary: Vivek Vikram Singh, MD and Group CEO of Sona BLW Precision Forgings (Sona Comstar), expects the company's annual investments to exceed the current ₹500-600 crore. The increased capital will focus on R&D, capacity expansion, and developing new capabilities and products as the firm scales operations.

articles.headline: Airlines schedule 2.6% fewer domestic flights for this Diwali month
articles.summary: Indian airlines are scheduled to operate 2.6% fewer domestic flights this Diwali month (November 2026) compared to October 2025, a reduction of 606 weekly flights. This adjustment comes amid elevated airfares due to increased fuel costs and rupee depreciation, leading to softer passenger demand, with Air India making the largest cuts.

articles.headline: Odisha lines up chip fab projects worth $4.7 billion
articles.summary: Odisha is advancing semiconductor projects valued at $4.7 billion, including chip fabrication and advanced 3D chip packaging units. This pivot aims to transform the state's industrial landscape from mining to microchips, with two India Semiconductor Mission-approved projects coming up in Odisha.

articles.headline: Traditional entry-level engg roles collapsed due to AI: LTM
articles.summary: Mid-tier IT services company LTM reports a collapse in traditional entry-level engineering roles (L0-L2) due to AI. AI-native thought processes and automation are compressing the software development life cycle, leading to demand for new skill sets like AI support engineers and architects, rather than conventional testing or quality assurance roles.

articles.headline: TW.O Capital raises $10 million to expand clean energy platform
articles.summary: Two Point O Capital (TW.O), an AI-powered clean energy deployment platform, secured $10 million in funding led by Transition Venture Capital. The investment will expand TW.O into battery energy storage and deepen its presence in solar, energy efficiency, and wastewater treatment for commercial and industrial businesses across India.

articles.headline: In a 1st, UPI average daily value crossed ~1 trn
articles.summary: The average daily value of Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions exceeded ₹1 trillion for the first time in October, coinciding with the festive season. October saw 25.47 billion transactions, up 23% year-on-year, with a total value of ₹31.53 trillion, 16% higher than October 2025.

articles.headline: Coal India fired up record supplies as Oct output jumped 19%
articles.summary: Coal India (CIL) achieved its highest-ever monthly coal supplies in October, exceeding 70 million tonnes (mt) for the first time, to meet rising power demand. October supplies of 70.3 mt marked a 19% increase year-on-year, and supplies to the power sector also reached an all-time monthly high of 57.1 mt.

articles.headline: EPFO launches WhatsApp services and automatic settlement of small accounts
articles.summary: EPFO introduced interactive WhatsApp-based services for subscribers to access PF account details and an automatic settlement facility for eligible inoperative accounts with balances up to ₹1,000. These initiatives aim to enhance digital service delivery and reduce physical visits, benefiting around 1 lakh accounts worth approximately ₹5 crore.

articles.headline: IBBI amends insolvency rules for stressed real estate developers
articles.summary: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI) amended insolvency rules for stressed real estate developers. The changes aim to promote viable resolution, enhance transparency, and protect homebuyers' interests, facilitating project-wise treatment and reducing information asymmetry in corporate insolvency resolution processes.

articles.headline: Cotton import duty exemption extended
articles.summary: The Centre extended the customs duty exemption on cotton imports until December 31, 2026. This decision, announced by the textile ministry, addresses the raw material requirements of the domestic textile industry, following a previous five-month exemption that ended October 31, 2026.

articles.headline: Sebi chief monitors Tata Group governance
articles.summary: Sebi Chief Tuhin Kanta Pandey stated that the markets regulator is monitoring governance developments within the Tata Group at the holding company level. He emphasized that the group’s listed companies and their promoters are subject to Sebi’s disclosure and compliance norms.

articles.headline: At Ramlila, Opposition closes ranks
articles.summary: The Congress-led INDIA bloc rallied at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan, protesting alleged "vote chori" (vote theft) through the Election Commission's electoral roll revision. Leaders accused the poll body of undermining democracy, facilitating wealth concentration, and demanded action against the CEC, alleging 130 million votes were deleted.

articles.headline: Silver lining for Keralam’s ageing population
articles.summary: Keralam is recasting elderly care as a social welfare and economic opportunity, with its population aged 60 and above at 20.7%. The state Assembly passed the Keralam Senior Citizens (Care and Protection of Rights) Bill, 2026, to build an ecosystem for older people, fostering a 'silver economy' and creating a potential blueprint for India.

articles.headline: India oil imports hit record in Oct
articles.summary: India's crude oil imports surged to a record 5.6 million barrels per day (bpd) in October, driven by refiners increasing purchases from West Asia and Russia. West Asian supplies accounted for 2.3 million bpd, while Russian crude flows remained strong at 2 million bpd, despite geopolitical tensions.

articles.headline: Diesel usage up 11%, LPG down 12% in Oct
articles.summary: India's petrol consumption increased 3.11% year-on-year to 3.77 million tonnes (mt) in October 2026, and diesel sales rose 11.69% to 8.51 mt. Conversely, LPG usage fell 12.11% to 2.64 mt, and aviation turbine fuel demand dropped 1.34% to 7.62 mt.

articles.headline: EAM meets Russia, S Korea counterparts
articles.summary: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar held separate meetings with his Russian, Polish, and South Korean counterparts on the sidelines of the G20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in Atlanta. Discussions covered the Ukraine conflict, the West Asia war, bilateral ties, and multilateral issues.

articles.headline: Mutilated bodies of two Manipur youth found
articles.summary: The mutilated bodies of two youths, missing for three days from Manipur’s Kangpokpi district, were discovered in Senapati. Security forces dispersed agitators protesting the killings, with Deputy Chief Minister Nemcha Kipgen condemning the incident.

articles.headline: IDBI employees to hold 2-day strike
articles.summary: IDBI Bank employees across over 2,000 branches will observe a two-day strike on November 2-3, 2026, to protest the bank’s privatization. The Uniter Forum of IDBI Officers & Employees Association asserts the bank's turnaround is due to public investment and employee efforts, raising concerns about public accountability.

articles.headline: Indigenous bullet train chugs along, squeeze tests underway
articles.summary: India’s indigenous bullet train program is progressing, with the B28 train set built by BEML undergoing final squeeze tests in Bengaluru. Designed for the Mumbai-Ahmedabad corridor, it will have a maximum test speed of 280 km/h and an operational speed of 249 km/h, with a passenger capacity of 557.

articles.headline: How it all unfolded: Inside the world’s largest crypto exchange
articles.summary: The $6.3 billion Binance hack unfolded on Thursday afternoon with unusual transactions alarming executives. The North Korean hacking unit TraderTraitor was identified as responsible. Binance halted withdrawals and deposits, with founder Changpeng Zhao promising to cover all losses, emphasizing that AI-driven hacking is a threat to the entire crypto industry.

articles.headline: Youth protests in Germany turn violent
articles.summary: Nationwide youth protests in Frankfurt, Germany, against underfunding of schools, cuts to social services, and rising living costs turned violent. Participants tried to break a weapons store window, reflecting widespread frustration among campaign group Gen Z regelt.

articles.headline: Russian strikes cut power to thousands in Ukraine
articles.summary: Russian strikes on Sunday left hundreds of thousands of Ukrainians without power, according to President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. Attacks hit power infrastructure in four Ukrainian regions overnight, while Russian authorities reported damage to an industrial site following Ukrainian drone attacks in Nizhny Novgorod.

articles.headline: Saudi GDP shrank 3.8% in Q3CY26
articles.summary: Saudi Arabia's economy contracted 3.8% year-on-year in Q3 CY26, an improvement from Q2's 4.7% contraction, but marking two straight periods of shrinkage since 2023. The non-oil sector grew 1.9%, while oil activities fell 20.4%, reflecting one of its worst economic performances in years.

articles.headline: S Korea export growth in Oct best since 1974
articles.summary: South Korea’s exports nearly doubled in October, rising 93.7% year-on-year to $115.28 billion, marking the sharpest jump in over 50 years. This performance, boosted by favorable calendar effects of more working days, surpassed market expectations and September’s 83.7% gain.

articles.headline: Protests rock France for a third weekend
articles.summary: Hundreds of thousands of protesters demonstrated across France for a third consecutive weekend over living costs and education. While largely peaceful, gatherings in Paris and other cities saw clouds of tear gas and scattered fires, despite authorities warning of a "very high risk" of disorder.

articles.headline: US midterms enter final leg
articles.summary: The US midterm elections are in their final stretch, with a record 50 million Americans having cast early ballots. Economic issues—including living costs, tariffs, and the Iran war—dominate the competitive battle for Congress, shaping the political discourse ahead of Tuesday's voting.

articles.headline: Pak LNG cargo hit near Hormuz had Iran approval
articles.summary: Pakistan negotiated with Iran to ensure safe passage for the LNG carrier Al Mayeda before it was attacked near the Strait of Hormuz. The Marshall Islands-flagged vessel, loaded with LNG from Qatar, came under fire, according to sources familiar with the situation.

articles.headline: Big Tech returns smallest share of cash to shareholders in 15 yrs
articles.summary: Four major US technology companies—Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, and Meta—returned only 9.3% of their generated cash to shareholders in the first nine months of 2026, the lowest in at least 15 years. This decline from 27.4% a year earlier is due to surging AI-related investments, squeezing share buybacks.

articles.headline: Time to revisit Narasimham report
articles.summary: A high-level committee formed to review India’s banking sector for 2047 aims to make it globally competitive and resilient. The author argues that recommendations from the 1991 Narasimham Committee on banking reforms, such as governance reforms for PSBs and a focused priority-sector lending framework, remain highly relevant and largely unfinished.

articles.headline: Go beyond banking
articles.summary: The Union government formed a high-level committee to review India’s banking sector and recommend regulatory, structural, and legislative reforms. This initiative aims to make the sector globally competitive and inclusive by 2047, addressing areas like prudential norms, capital requirements, priority-sector lending, and AI integration, amidst a large unmet demand for credit.

articles.headline: AI capex boom
articles.summary: Four tech giants (Google, Meta, Amazon, Microsoft) lost $900 billion in market value after Q3 FY27 results, primarily due to increased AI-related capital expenditure. Google’s free cash flow turned negative due to massive investments in AI models like Gemini, which is cannibalizing its search business and impacting ad revenue, raising investor concerns about AI investment sustainability.

articles.headline: Yes, blame the state
articles.summary: The article argues that systemic problems in India are often attributed to individual behavior, but the root cause lies in state failures. It emphasizes that a capable state creates conditions for societal progress through effective governance, infrastructure, and institutions, citing examples from Singapore, Japan, and South Korea, where state intervention shaped economic success.

articles.headline: Buying a home abroad? Be prepared to tackle tax and legal hurdles
articles.summary: More Indians are buying overseas property, now accounting for 13% of surveyed buyers' wealth. Buyers must assess budgets from ₹1 crore to over ₹10 crore, considering destinations like Thailand, UK, and US. Key risks include policy changes, inheritance rules, unfamiliar tax regimes like Firpta, and compliance with Indian LRS norms and income tax obligations.

articles.headline: Insurance cheque sent by post: Which date matters?
articles.summary: The article clarifies that for insurance premiums paid by cheque, the date of payment relates back to the date the cheque was received by the insurer, provided it's not dishonoured. This is based on a Supreme Court ruling, emphasizing Section 64VB of the Insurance Act and the importance of retaining a photocopy of the cheque.

articles.headline: NavIC revival puts focus on India’s private space might
articles.summary: ISRO’s successful launch of NVS-03 revitalizes India’s NavIC system, critical after IRNSS-1F's atomic clock failure. The mission highlights growing private sector involvement, with 80% of ISRO’s launch budget channeled to domestic companies. Hyderabad-based Ananth Technologies contributed significantly, underscoring India's self-reliance in advanced space systems.

articles.headline: IN-SPACe offers ~67 crore to four firms
articles.summary: The Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre (IN-SPACe) granted financial support totaling ₹67.15 crore to four firms: Manastu Space, IMumbai Semiconductor, Inspecity Space Laboratories, and AeroDome Technologies. This funding will facilitate the development of indigenous technologies for satellite propulsion, in-orbit servicing, and precision timing systems.

articles.headline: NMACC opens The Library, pairing books, art, food with readings
articles.summary: The Nita Mukesh Ambani Cultural Centre (NMACC) launched "The Library," a cultural space combining literature, art, design, and food. It features varied book collections, a coffee bar, a stage for events like book readings, and integrated dining. The space aims to encourage visitors to linger and explore, connecting diverse art forms.

articles.headline: AI could be the force multiplier
articles.summary: India’s ambition for a $30 trillion economy by 2047 necessitates substantial growth and reinvention in its public-sector banking (PSB) sector. AI is proposed as a force multiplier, driving shifts in customer primacy, productivity, financial inclusion, workforce augmentation, and trust architecture to enable PSBs to meet future demands.

articles.headline: Improved cross-border payment infra still has a long way to go
articles.summary: Movin Jain, cofounder of Skydo Technologies, notes significant improvements in cross-border payment infrastructure but emphasizes a long way to go for SMEs. Delays stem from varying regulatory structures, bank processes, and manual compliance checks, necessitating automation in compliance, forex conversion, and reconciliation to achieve 24/7 payment systems.

articles.headline: A crisis with benefits
articles.summary: The 2018 unspooling of IL&FS led to significant changes in India's corporate legal and regulatory landscape, including the establishment of the NFRA and a framework for group insolvencies. Recoveries are now set to exceed initial commitments, with ₹50,387 crore repaid by July 2026, demonstrating how administrative and business leadership can resolve complex boardroom crises.

articles.headline: INDIA Bloc holds 'Vote Bachao' rally against alleged voter list manipulation
articles.summary: Leaders from the INDIA bloc, including Rahul Gandhi and Mamata Banerjee, gathered at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan. They accused the BJP-led government of "vote chori" and undermining democracy. Rahul Gandhi claimed 15% of voters were deleted from 2024 lists to influence results. The BJP dismissed the event as a "flop show" and criticized its timing on the anniversary of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots.

articles.headline: Karnataka government considers granting official status to yellow-and-red state flag
articles.summary: CM DK Shivakumar announced that Karnataka is exploring legal options to grant official recognition to the yellow-and-red Kannada flag as a state symbol. He clarified the move would not affect the dignity of the National Tricolour. The government also plans to make hoisting the flag mandatory at government offices and aided institutions to promote regional identity and language pride.

articles.headline: India's GST collections jump 23% in October to record Rs 2.3L crore
articles.summary: GST collections hit a record high of Rs 2.3 lakh crore in October 2026, marking a 23% increase. The growth was driven by a surge in quarter-end demand and robust domestic sales during the festive season. Collections from imports saw a significant 42% rise. Meghalaya and Himachal Pradesh recorded the highest growth among states, signaling strong consumption across various economic sectors.

articles.headline: Over 127 plots in Bengaluru sold then illegally mortgaged to scam-hit bank
articles.summary: Residents of Sri Shankara Layout discovered 127 plots they already owned were mortgaged to Sri Guru Raghavendra Sahakara Bank for loans totaling Rs 961 crore. The mortgage deeds were executed in 2019, years after the plots were sold to individual buyers. The bank administrator is investigating the fraud, while owners fear for their physical possession and legal rights to the properties.

articles.headline: Bengaluru pubs emerge as 'third spaces' for intellectual and philosophical debates
articles.summary: A growing trend in Bengaluru sees bars and pubs hosting 'lectures over drinks' as alternative learning hubs. Events like 'Pint of View' and 'Intellect on Ice' attract young professionals for talks on AI, philosophy, and science. Organizers argue these venues bridge the gap between academic institutions and the public, providing a relaxed social environment for discovering new ideas.

articles.headline: Classic Mysore pak reimagined with modern twists in Karnataka's culinary scene
articles.summary: The traditional Mysore pak is undergoing a transformation as local cafes and confectioners introduce variants like cheesecake, craft chocolate, and filter coffee infusions. While legacy brands maintain authenticity, new-age kitchens target urban consumers with jaggery-based and portion-controlled options. The shift reflects changing dynamics as customers seek lighter or fusion versions.

articles.headline: Nagarathpet remains Bengaluru's midnight food hub amid heritage trading lanes
articles.summary: Nagarathpet, one of Bengaluru's oldest markets, continues to thrive as a street food destination after shop shutters close at night. Famous for its bath masala dosa and badam milk, the area blends centuries-old trading traditions with a vibrant night-time appetite. The lanes attract traders and food lovers, maintaining a unique cultural identity in the city's historic heart.

articles.headline: Two thousand students showcase Karnataka's heritage at 71st Rajyotsava event
articles.summary: The 71st Kannada Rajyotsava was celebrated at Bengaluru's Kanteerava Stadium with 2,000 students performing dances depicting the state's literary icons and history. CM DK Shivakumar hoisted the national and state flags, urging the youth to preserve the Kannada language. The event featured cultural tableaus and performances highlighting government initiatives like free textbooks and meals.

articles.headline: CCTV footage suggests electrical fault near entrance led to hotel pool deaths
articles.summary: Investigation into the electrocution of two foreign nationals at Bengaluru's Conrad Hotel suggests a possible electrical fault near the pool entrance railings. CCTV shows a victim struggling after swimming near LED lighting. The Karnataka Swimming Association plans to issue comprehensive safety guidelines covering earthing, maintenance, and first-aid for all state pool operators.

articles.headline: Former Rangayana director ink-attacked during Mahatma Gandhi play in Bengaluru
articles.summary: Addanda Cariappa, former director of Mysuru Rangayana, was attacked with ink by protesters during a play about Mahatma Gandhi’s assassination. Protesters alleged the play portrayed Gandhi negatively and was anti-national. Cariappa filed a counter-complaint alleging assault and disruption. Police are investigating both claims amid tensions over the play's portrayal of historical events.

articles.headline: Volunteers and students lead green drives across Bengaluru for Rajyotsava
articles.summary: Around 250 volunteers marked the 71st Kannada Rajyotsava with green drives at neighborhood parks and Kasturinagar lake. Organized by groups like the Indian Ploggers Army, the initiative involved weed clearance and sapling care. The drive aimed to inspire social responsibility and environmental awareness among students and citizens while celebrating the state’s foundation day.

articles.headline: Congress considers early local body elections to counter recent council setbacks
articles.summary: Following a clean sweep by the BJP-JD(S) alliance in legislative council elections, the Congress party in Karnataka is weighing early panchayat and Greater Bengaluru Authority polls. The move aims to demonstrate organizational strength and blunt opposition claims of rising power. A win could rebuild confidence among party functionaries ahead of the 2028 assembly elections.

articles.headline: Karnataka minister objects to Maharashtra’s floodwater diversion project in Krishna basin
articles.summary: Karnataka Industries Minister MB Patil opposed Maharashtra's proposal to divert 40 tmc feet of floodwater from the Krishna river to the Bhima river. He warned the Rs 19,000 crore project would harm Karnataka's interests and reduce inflows into the Almatti dam. Patil urged the Centre to clarify the legal basis for the project, noting it falls outside existing tribunal awards.

articles.headline: New police circular mandates prior approval for interrogating registration department staff
articles.summary: DG&IGP MA Saleem issued a circular directing police to obtain necessary approvals before summoning registration department staff for property fraud inquiries. The directive follows complaints of harassment and mandates that staff be treated as witnesses during preliminary probes. Statements should be recorded at locations of their choice to avoid unnecessary complications.

articles.headline: Chainsaw attack survivor undergoes 20-hour surgery, remains in critical condition
articles.summary: A 14-year-old girl attacked with a chainsaw by her cousin in Andhra Pradesh is in critical condition after 20 hours of surgery in Bengaluru. Doctors used 114 boxes of surgical thread to treat multiple severe cuts to her face and upper body. The victim suffered significant blood loss and remains on ventilator support. Her willpower to recover has been described as courageous by doctors.

articles.headline: Final land acquisition notification issued for 1,895 acres for Bidadi township
articles.summary: The Karnataka government issued a final notification to acquire 1,895 acres for the Greater Bengaluru Integrated Township in Bidadi. The project, using a work-live-play model, has faced 18 months of farmer protests. Compensation will be determined under the 2013 Land Acquisition Act, with options for developed sites. The project has been exempted from some rehabilitation benefits.

articles.headline: Exhibition in Bengaluru revives forgotten Jala loom weaving tradition from Molakalmuru
articles.summary: A new exhibition titled "Pampa" at NGMA Bengaluru showcases the revival of the Jala loom technique, which had disappeared from Molakalmuru. The effort was inspired by a sari in a Paris museum that shared similarities with local traditions. The exhibition features over 150 textiles and installations, tracing Karnataka’s handmade textile heritage since the 18th century.

articles.headline: Southeast Asian drug cartels use barter system for illicit trade in Northeast
articles.summary: An ED investigation revealed drug syndicates from the Golden Triangle are using a barter system to smuggle heroin and meth into India through Mizoram. Instead of cash, payments are made with fuel, food, and medicines. Illegal funds from Indian cities are converted into marketable goods to leave no money trail. Over 1,400 mule accounts have been frozen in connection with the network.

articles.headline: Rajasthan medical college expels 13 students for ragging first-year juniors
articles.summary: Government Medical College in Barmer, Rajasthan, expelled 13 MBBS students from the hostel permanently and disciplined 66 others for ragging. Juniors alleged they were forced to keep short hair and submit prescribed introductions. The action followed a zero-tolerance policy. The National Medical Commission has received 12 similar complaints of ragging and harassment this year.

articles.headline: Goa lab develops bioinspired fish-like robots for non-invasive deep-sea studies
articles.summary: The National Institute of Oceanography in Goa is developing underwater robots that mimic marine animals. Unlike traditional vehicles with noisy propellers, these "BURs" use soft, flexible materials and smart sensors to study deep-sea environments without disrupting aquatic life. The robots are designed to withstand high pressure and sample water for chemical pollutants and salinity.

articles.headline: Anti-dam group in Arunachal calls Siang bandh over activist arrests
articles.summary: The SUMP Affected Area Youth Association called for a total shutdown in three Arunachal districts starting Monday. The group is demanding the release of over 40 protesters arrested following violence against the proposed 11,200MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project. Tensions escalated after activists attacked security personnel during earlier anti-dam demonstrations in the region.

articles.headline: Bodies of two abducted Kuki youths found in Manipur's Kangpokpi district
articles.summary: The bodies of two Kuki youths, missing since October 28, were found in gunny bags in a banana plantation in Manipur. The discovery triggered fresh protests and an extension of a total shutdown in the Kuki-majority district. Local organizations accused Naga militants of the abduction. The deaths deepen the ongoing ethnic conflict which has claimed over 300 lives since May 2023.

articles.headline: Private medical colleges offer 40% fee discount as 3,426 seats remain vacant
articles.summary: Private medical colleges are offering up to 40% discounts on tuition fees as thousands of MBBS seats remain unfilled after multiple counseling rounds. The vacancy is attributed to exorbitant fee structures reaching Rs 1.25 crore for the full course. Experts say the mismatch between high costs and student affordability has created an institutional crisis in the private medical sector.

articles.headline: NCTE launches MITRA and PUSHTI initiatives to elevate teaching standards
articles.summary: The National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE) introduced two new frameworks, MITRA and PUSHTI, to improve school education. MITRA connects teachers with experienced mentors for professional support, while PUSHTI sets standards for holistic teaching competencies. The initiatives aim to provide continuous professional development in line with National Education Policy 2020 objectives.

articles.headline: India’s extreme poverty rate drops to 2.6% over twelve-year period
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi cited World Bank data showing India's extreme poverty rate collapsed from 27.1% in 2011 to 2.6% in 2023. Nearly 50 crore people moved out of poverty during this period. The PM also highlighted that employment grew by 13.4 crore between 2017 and 2023, while income inequality, measured by the Gini index, fell by over 20% during the same timeframe.

articles.headline: Election Commission to ease SIR portal restrictions after judicial objections
articles.summary: The Election Commission is likely to modify its portal to allow judges of the SIR tribunal to consider more than the 13 specified documents during appeals. The move follows a month-long deadlock in West Bengal where judges argued portal restrictions violated their mandate. The EC will also introduce digital signatures for authentication instead of Aadhaar credentials.

articles.headline: Himalayan Black Bear recorded preying on endangered red panda for first time
articles.summary: Researchers from the Wildlife Institute of India documented the first verified photographic evidence of an Asiatic black bear preying on a red panda in Singalila National Park. Experts suggest shortening hibernation periods and food scarcity may be altering the seasonal diet of bears. No such predation event has been reported earlier across the red panda's global range.

articles.headline: New Air Force Chief prioritizes restoring sanctioned fighter squadron strength
articles.summary: Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, upon taking charge, stated that restoring the IAF’s fighter strength is his foremost task. With combat squadrons down to 29 against a sanctioned 42, he emphasized accelerating indigenous programs like the Tejas Mk1A and the AMCA. He also highlighted the need to adapt to new technologies including drones, AI, and long-range precision weapons.

articles.headline: Six Indian trekkers stranded in Nepal's snowbound Upper Dolpa region
articles.summary: A group of six Indian trekkers are stranded near Shey-Phoksundo Lake in Nepal after ignoring weather warnings. Heavy snowfall from Cyclone Arnab made trails impassable, and a technical fault in a rescue helicopter delayed evacuation efforts. The group reportedly left their guide behind to press ahead despite warnings of high-altitude rain and avalanche risks from local authorities.

articles.headline: CAG flags failure to transfer Rs 3L crore crude oil cess to fund
articles.summary: The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) reported that Rs 2.93 lakh crore collected as cess on crude oil by the central government was not transferred to the designated oil industry development fund. The auditor noted this was due to the non-creation of the fund until recent intervention. The CAG emphasized the importance of access to digital records and government databases for audits.

articles.headline: Over 100 police officers injured in German protests against living costs
articles.summary: Riots broke out in Frankfurt, Cologne, and Berlin following youth-led protests demanding government investment in housing and education. Over 100 police officers were injured and 54 people were detained after shops were looted. Organizers distanced themselves from the violence, which drew over 100,000 participants demanding measures to make daily life more affordable.

articles.headline: EPFO pumps Rs 17,000 crore into equities during first quarter of FY27
articles.summary: The Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) invested nearly Rs 17,000 crore in fresh equity during the April-June quarter, raising its total exposure to 11.2%. The shift towards stocks is part of a strategy to generate higher returns for its 30 crore members amid lower yields on government securities. Short-term debt and central government bonds remain the largest asset classes.

articles.headline: Bank of Baroda scales up cybersecurity spending after July data attack
articles.summary: Following a cyberattack in July 2026, state-run Bank of Baroda increased its IT defense spending to over 10% of its operating profit. The bank is upgrading its technology framework, personnel training, and operational processes to prevent future breaches. The investment will be spread across the current and next fiscal years to ensure a robust digital defense for its customers.

articles.headline: Manisha Bhanwala makes history with world wrestling title in Astana
articles.summary: Manisha Bhanwala became a world champion by winning the 59kg title at the senior world wrestling championships in Astana. Her victory adds to the legacy of the Sir Chhotu Ram Akhara in Rohtak, which has produced several Olympic and world medalists. Manisha, who also works as a state coach, was lauded for her dedication and for overcoming ground game weaknesses to win the historic title.

articles.headline: Diljit Dosanjh kicks off tour in Delhi amid 'Artist' phrase controversy
articles.summary: Singer Diljit Dosanjh performed to a crowd of 80,000 in Delhi to launch his latest tour. During the show, he addressed the controversy regarding his "I am an artist, bro" response to political questions, stating he owns the phrase with pride and has only love for his fans and critics. The concert featured bhangra, grand entries, and a laser display celebrating his artistic identity.

articles.headline: Priyanka Chopra Jonas joins Indian short film 'We Were Here' as producer
articles.summary: Priyanka Chopra Jonas joined filmmaker Pranav Bhasin’s Oscar-qualified short film "We Were Here" as an executive producer. The film, which also features Andrew Scott on the production team, has already won over 20 international awards. Chopra stated she came on board to amplify the creative vision of the witty take on timely subjects as the film heads for Academy Award consideration.

articles.headline: Rising smartphone prices drive 100% growth for refurbished device market
articles.summary: High costs of new smartphones are pushing Indian consumers toward refurbished alternatives, with retailers like ControlZ and Cashify reporting 100% growth. The secondary market is thriving even as new handset sales slow. Older iPhone models, particularly the 13, 14, and 15 series, are most popular. The trend is expanding into smaller cities where trade-in activity has grown by nearly 50%.

articles.headline: Large factories drive 72% of India's manufacturing output despite low numbers
articles.summary: A study shows India's manufacturing sector is fragmented, with just 10% of factories—those with over 200 workers—generating 72% of gross value added. Conversely, smaller units make up 71% of operational factories but contribute only 10% to output. The divide is attributed to differences in R&D investment, skill training, and credit access between large and small establishments.

articles.headline: CEC stole citizens’ voice, will go to jail: Rahul Gandhi
articles.summary: Rahul Gandhi accused Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar of "treason" for stealing citizens' voice, stating he would be removed and jailed. He spoke at an INDIA bloc rally in Delhi protesting alleged electoral irregularities, outlining a post-Modi vision of harmony.

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh braces for second cyclone, Murasu, within a week
articles.summary: Andhra Pradesh is preparing for Cyclone Murasu, expected to make landfall on Tuesday, just a week after Cyclone Arnab. Five districts are on red alert, expecting heavy rain and winds up to 120 kmph between Nellore and Narsapur. Tamil Nadu and Odisha are also bracing for impact.

articles.headline: GST collection surges 23% on festive demand to ₹2.31 lakh cr.
articles.summary: Goods and Services Tax (GST) collections jumped 23% year-on-year to over ₹2.31 lakh crore in October, driven by festive buying and increased domestic demand. This is the second consecutive month exceeding ₹2 lakh crore, with revenues from imports climbing 42%.

articles.headline: Unemployment falls but ‘decent work’ still scarce in India
articles.summary: India's unemployment rate fell from 6.1% (2017-18) to 3.2% (2023-24), with increased female workforce participation. However, "decent work" remains scarce due to informal employment, insecure arrangements, and limited social security access, impacting economic growth and increasing inequality.

articles.headline: Indian Navy to launch ₹80,000-crore next-generation destroyer project
articles.summary: The government approved Project 18A, an ₹80,000-crore project for the Indian Navy to develop next-generation stealth-guided missile destroyers. This push addresses growing maritime security challenges from China and Pakistan, aiming for 75% indigenous content in the warships.

articles.headline: Delhi CM announces plan to turn Netaji Subhash Marg into heritage corridor
articles.summary: Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta announced a plan to redevelop the 3.3-km Netaji Subhash Marg, connecting Delhi Gate to Kashmere Gate, into an organised, attractive heritage corridor. The project aims to integrate history, architecture, and modern urban life, focusing on green spaces and heritage sites.

articles.headline: BJP rallies over anti-Sikh riots, demands Congress apology
articles.summary: Hours before the INDIA bloc rally, BJP held a protest march in Delhi demanding a Congress apology for the 1984 anti-Sikh riots. Union Minister Hardeep Singh Puri and CM Rekha Gupta stated the tragedy must not be forgotten and justice is still sought.

articles.headline: Jadavpur University V-C orders probe into molestation complaint
articles.summary: Jadavpur University's Vice-Chancellor ordered a probe after a first-year student reported being molested by a non-teaching staffer on campus on Friday. The complaint details the staffer allegedly pulling her hand and touching her inappropriately after an altercation.

articles.headline: Azam Khan sent to 14-day judicial custody in money laundering case
articles.summary: Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan was remanded in 14-day judicial custody by a Ghaziabad court in a money laundering case. The ED's investigation stems from 26 FIRs alleging forcible occupation of farmers' land for Mohammad Ali Jauhar University and diversion of public funds.

articles.headline: Chainsaw attack accused critical after police firing in Andhra Pradesh
articles.summary: M. Hemanth, accused in a chainsaw attack on a Class X student, was critically injured in police firing in Andhra Pradesh's Atmakur forest. He allegedly resisted arrest and attempted to attack an officer, prompting police to open fire. IT Minister Nara Lokesh visited the victim.

articles.headline: IIT-B student death: candlelight march held for justice
articles.summary: Student organizations and residents held a candlelight march in Mumbai for Sahil Wakode, an IIT Bombay student who allegedly died by suicide. Participants demanded justice and expressed solidarity with his parents, who are on hunger strike.

articles.headline: Bihar Opposition attacks BJP after 2 Independent MLCs 'join' ruling party
articles.summary: Bihar Opposition parties demanded disqualification of two newly elected Independent MLCs, Bansidhar Brajwasi and Rahul Raj, after the BJP issued a statement welcoming them. The BJP later clarified they only "extended support." RJD MP Manoj Kumar Jha accused them of violating anti-defection law.

articles.headline: Bengaluru's final electoral rolls riddled with errors
articles.summary: Bengaluru's final electoral rolls contain numerous errors, from garbled names like "XXX" or "?????K" to single letters, email IDs, or "NA" entries in place of relatives' names. Discrepancies were found in at least 1,000 entries, with officials attributing issues to transliteration errors.

articles.headline: Bengal CM targets 2.5 lakh Matua citizenships under CAA by Dec. 31
articles.summary: West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari announced a target to grant citizenship certificates to 2.5 lakh Matuas under the CAA by December 31. He stated the state government would expedite applications and include new citizens in the voter list by January 2027.

articles.headline: A.P. civic polls peaceful; Jagan demands repoll in Pulivendula
articles.summary: Elections for 13 municipal corporations and 79 municipalities in Andhra Pradesh were largely peaceful, with 48.03% polling. YSRCP president Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy staged a protest in Pulivendula, demanding a repoll due to alleged electoral malpractices and left without voting.

articles.headline: Submit doctors' credentials, HC tells Delhi govt. and NMC
articles.summary: The Delhi High Court gave NMC and Delhi government two weeks to submit a joint inquiry report on the medical qualifications of two doctors accused of mishandling a child's treatment. This order came during a contempt petition hearing.

articles.headline: AMU women students denied voting rights in students’ union polls
articles.summary: About 4,000 women students at AMU's Women’s College are denied voting rights in AMUSU elections, raising concerns over gender discrimination. Despite paying union fees and living on campus, they cannot vote, a decision justified by "geographical distance" and a separate women's union.

articles.headline: Academia's challenge: Balancing teaching and research
articles.summary: Higher education institutions face challenges balancing teaching and research. The NEP 2020 categorizes three types of institutions. Research is increasingly valued for ranking, but brilliant teachers aren't always researchers, and vice-versa. Finding a balance is crucial for advancing knowledge.

articles.headline: Chandigarh to be India's first drug-free city: Amit Shah
articles.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah declared Chandigarh will be India's first drug-free city, reiterating the Centre's resolve for a drug-free India. He noted Chandigarh Police increased conviction rates in NDPS cases to 93% and registered 8,206 FIRs since August 4, 2024.

articles.headline: Congress protecting '3 crore infiltrators', CEC protest a 'foolish drama': Nadda
articles.summary: BJP chief Nitin Nadda accused Congress of protecting "3 crore infiltrators" and termed the INDIA bloc's protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar a "foolish drama." He linked Congress to the 1984 anti-Sikh riots, stating their politics involved "lying and spreading rumours."

articles.headline: Thousands attend INDIA bloc rally in Delhi, protest 'vote theft'
articles.summary: Thousands from across India attended the INDIA bloc rally in Delhi, protesting alleged "vote theft" and electoral roll deletions. Despite travel restrictions and logistical challenges, attendees expressed anger over perceived government wrongdoings and sought political change.

articles.headline: Protesters leave trail of graffiti, litter on roads to Ramlila Maidan
articles.summary: Following the INDIA bloc rally, central Delhi roads and walls leading to Ramlila Maidan were littered with dust, banners, food wrappers, and empty bottles. Protesters also spray-painted slogans, with waste collectors gathering recyclables while others expressed commitment to the protest.

articles.headline: West Bengal govt. notifies jobs for kin of political violence victims
articles.summary: The West Bengal government issued a notification providing Group D jobs for family members of those killed in political violence since 2001. This one-time exception, announced by CM Suvendu Adhikari, aims to provide employment and requires proof of incident and income below ₹50,000.

articles.headline: FPIs pull out ₹34,843 crore from Indian equities in October
articles.summary: Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) withdrew ₹34,843 crore from Indian equities in October, the second consecutive month of heavy outflows. Concerns over higher crude oil prices, global interest rates, and corporate earnings drove the outflows, though net buying resumed late-month.

articles.headline: Six Indian tourists stranded in Nepal, rescue operation under way
articles.summary: Six Indian tourists, including two women, are stranded in heavy snowfall in Nepal's Shey-Phoksundo National Park area since Saturday. Officials located them, and an Army helicopter is en route for rescue. Tourists ventured despite warnings.

articles.headline: Why make litigants rush to SC for early hearings, CJI asks High Courts
articles.summary: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant flagged a "growing tendency" of litigants approaching the Supreme Court for urgent hearing directions in High Court cases. He noted 65,54,788 cases pending in High Courts and 97,201 in the Supreme Court, questioning responsiveness of processes.

articles.headline: Labour Minister calls on EPFO to evolve with the times
articles.summary: Union Labour Minister Mansukh Mandaviya urged EPFO employees to focus on worker-centric innovations and adapt processes. Speaking on EPFO's 74th Foundation Day, he highlighted the organization's ₹32 lakh crore corpus and the need for human sensitivity in social security.

articles.headline: Bengal STF busts inter-State drug network, four arrested
articles.summary: West Bengal Police STF busted an inter-State drug network in Malda district, arresting four individuals and recovering 2.688 kg of morphine worth about ₹3 crore. The operation was part of an ongoing crackdown on narcotics syndicates.

articles.headline: Search for eight missing trekkers in Uttarakhand under way
articles.summary: SDRF launched a search and rescue operation for seven trekkers and one guide missing on the Kedartal trek in Uttarakhand due to heavy snowfall. A group of 13 had set out on October 27. Aerial reconnaissance by helicopter is planned.

articles.headline: Bhutan builds 108 stupas in 9 hours, dedicates one to Modi
articles.summary: Bhutan's King Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuk dedicated Chorten Number 76, part of 108 Buddhist stupas built in a nine-hour feat, to PM Narendra Modi. This gesture appreciates India's support for Bhutan's Gelephu Mindfulness City project.

articles.headline: Playbook to overcome inflation in personal finance
articles.summary: Inflation erodes buying power, requiring alignment of spending, saving, and investing with price trends. India's CPI averaged 5% last decade. Strategies include tracking personal inflation, cutting waste, and using inflation-resilient investments like diversified equity, debt funds, and gold.

articles.headline: Gold, silver lose sheen; outlook turns negative
articles.summary: Gold and silver clocked negative returns for the second consecutive month in October. Comex gold fell 7.26% to $3,884.9/ounce, and Comex silver dropped 19.1% to $49.13/ounce, impacted by crude oil prices, inflation, and potential U.S. interest rate hikes.

articles.headline: No-cost EMI is a loan, not truly free, warn experts
articles.summary: "No-cost EMI" is often a disguised loan, where banks charge interest and GST, with retailers recovering costs via higher prices or loss of discounts. The real interest rate can be 18-20%. Consumers are advised to compare cash prices and assess affordability without EMI.

articles.headline: Iran warns new war could last longer after Trump threats
articles.summary: Iran warned that any renewed war with the U.S. could last longer, and the U.S. President wouldn't dictate its conclusion. This follows Donald Trump's suggestion of swift strikes on remaining targets. Revolutionary Guards warned of "no geographic limitations" in conflict.

articles.headline: Lula's historic win in Brazil faces humongous challenges
articles.summary: Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva secured a remarkable comeback win in Brazil's presidential election with 51.79% of the vote. His victory is seen as a beacon of hope for progressive forces in Latin America and multilateralism, but he faces significant challenges at home with a fragmented Congress.

articles.headline: France launches 'attempted murder' probe over protest attacks
articles.summary: France opened an attempted murder probe after petrol bombs were thrown at security forces during Paris protests against soaring living costs. Footage showed an officer engulfed in flames, prompting outrage. Prosecutors cited "extraordinary" violence by rioters.

articles.headline: Terrorism a 'red line', Pakistan warns Afghanistan of action
articles.summary: Pakistan warned Afghanistan that it reserves the right to eliminate cross-border terror threats, calling terrorism a "red line" and national security non-negotiable. This follows Afghan Taliban's refusal to address militancy and shift blame.

articles.headline: Milne, Seifert secure New Zealand T20I win over India
articles.summary: Tim Seifert scored 93 off 50 balls, and Adam Milne took 4/19, leading New Zealand to a seven-wicket win over India in the final T20I. India, however, clinched the five-match series 3-2. The win was Shreyas Iyer's first series victory in a SENA country as captain.

articles.headline: Manav Thakkar wins first international table tennis crown
articles.summary: India's Manav Thakkar won his maiden international men’s singles title at WTT Feeder Chennai, recovering from a two-game deficit to beat England's Samuel Walker 6-11, 8-11, 11-9, 11-3, 11-8. South Korea's Yoo Yerin won the women's singles, with Sutirtha Mukherjee as runner-up.

articles.headline: Havertz helps Arsenal break Anfield hoodoo, top Premier League
articles.summary: Arsenal moved top of the Premier League with their first win away to Liverpool in 14 years, secured by Kai Havertz’s early strike for a 1-0 victory. Real Madrid beat Racing Santander 3-0, while Barcelona thrashed Alaves 6-1 in LaLiga.

articles.headline: Delhi, Services battle for Ranji Trophy knockout spot
articles.summary: Delhi and Services will clash in the Ranji Trophy, with both teams needing an outright victory to stay in knockout contention. Services, despite being the designated visitor, enjoys greater familiarity with the Palam 'A' ground conditions.

articles.headline: Services cricketers seek exposure to State-based T20 leagues
articles.summary: Services skipper Rajat Paliwal expressed desire for his cricketers from the Indian Army, Navy, and Air Force to gain exposure in State-based T20 leagues. He believes this initiative would improve player quality, preparation, and provide valuable experience.

articles.headline: Delhi won't host India-Lanka ODI due to stadium renovation
articles.summary: Delhi will not host India’s ODI against Sri Lanka on December 13 due to ongoing renovation of the outfield at the Arun Jaitley Stadium. The stadium's sand-based outfield renovation will take around four months, delaying its readiness for cricket until the 2027 IPL.

articles.headline: Parikh, Paes to contest AITA elections under ‘Tennis First’ banner
articles.summary: Incumbent president Chintan Parikh and Leander Paes will contest the AITA elections on November 27 under the 'Tennis First' banner. Parikh seeks re-election as president, while Paes will run for vice-president, aiming for reforms in Indian tennis administration.

articles.headline: Indian men and women reign supreme in Commonwealth kabaddi
articles.summary: Indian men's and women's teams dominated the inaugural Commonwealth kabaddi championship, winning titles in one-sided finals in Ahmedabad. The women defeated Uganda 35-15, and the men beat Sri Lanka 54-20, showcasing emphatic performances.

articles.headline: Lifter Usha tops 61kg Group D at World Weightlifting championships
articles.summary: Indian weightlifter Usha topped Group D in the women’s 61kg category at the IWF World championships in Ningbo, China, lifting a total of 212kg (93kg snatch, 119kg clean and jerk). Compatriot Nirupama Devi finished fourth in Group C with 211kg.

articles.headline: Alcaraz beats de Minaur to win Vienna Open tennis title
articles.summary: Carlos Alcaraz defeated Alex de Minaur 6-1, 6-4 to win the Vienna Open, marking his seventh victory against de Minaur. This was the Spaniard’s fourth title of the year, including the Australian Open, and his 28th overall.

articles.headline: 'Canelo' Alvarez wins back WBC crown from Mbilli
articles.summary: Saul "Canelo" Alvarez defeated French fighter Christian Mbilli in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, to regain his WBC super middleweight title. The 36-year-old Mexican won a 12-round decision, exerting his influence in the fight's second half.

articles.headline: Marc Marquez on verge of clinching World MotoGP title
articles.summary: Marc Marquez moved closer to his eighth world title with a dominant victory at the Malaysian MotoGP. The Ducati star won ahead of Pedro Acosta and Alex Marquez, now leading the standings with 399 points, followed by Martin (355) and Bezzecchi (332).

articles.headline: ISL: SC Delhi rallies to beat Mumbai City again
articles.summary: SC Delhi netted three goals in the final 20 minutes to stage a 3-2 comeback victory over Mumbai City FC in an Indian Super League match, completing a double over them. Carlos Fortes, Akshat Mehra, and Juan Pena scored for Delhi after trailing 0-2 at half-time.

articles.headline: Chiranth Vishwanath completes double in national motorsports
articles.summary: Chiranth Vishwanath secured a double victory in the Super Sport 301-400cc Open class at the MRF Indian National Racing Challenge 2W, beating rival Sarthak Chavan. Savion Sabu also completed a double in the Pro-Stock 200cc Open class.

articles.headline: Steep learning curve for young cricketer Vaibhav Sooryavanshi
articles.summary: Young cricketer Vaibhav Sooryavanshi faces a "steep learning curve" after being benched in the T20I series against New Zealand despite a brilliant 45 off 19 balls. India's policy of sticking with its core players means he must continue performing well in domestic cricket to press his claims.

articles.headline: El Niño doesn't always guarantee a poor Indian monsoon
articles.summary: A strong El Niño doesn't always mean a poor Indian monsoon. While most moderate/strong El Niños since 1950 led to deficient rainfall, 1997 saw normal levels due to a positive Indian Ocean Dipole and other atmospheric factors. IMD's forecasting has improved significantly since.

articles.headline: 'Hell chicken' dinosaur ate fruits, study suggests
