articles.summary: A new Nature Communications study suggests the bird-like dinosaur Infernogallus jamesi, a toothless theropod from the Hell Creek Formation, ate fleshy fruits. CT scans revealed its jaw could slide forwards/backwards, resembling fruit-eating parrots, coinciding with flowering plants evolving fruit.

articles.headline: Oil spill spreads along UAE coast, beaches closed
articles.summary: An oil spill from a tanker attacked near the Strait of Hormuz has spread along the UAE coastline. Sharjah has temporarily closed all public beaches as a precaution.

articles.headline: KKR, Singtel, Tata Comms Explore Sale of STT Global Data Centres India
articles.summary: KKR, Singtel, and Tata Communications are exploring the sale of STT Global Data Centres India for over $5.5 billion. This dual-track initiative, alongside an earlier IPO plan, aims to rebalance capital requirements and streamline data centre operations. The company has 34 data centers with 613 MW capacity.

articles.headline: Digital Payment Firms Boost Security Amid Rising Cyberattacks
articles.summary: Digital payment companies like PhonePe, Razorpay, Cashfree, and PayU are strengthening cybersecurity systems, automating responses, and implementing stricter transaction checks due to increased cyberattacks. AI tools are being deployed for security analysis and real-time fraud detection. Attacks have risen tenfold compared to a year ago.

articles.headline: India's Macro Indicators Rise on Strong Demand, Festive Season Boost
articles.summary: India's strong consumption story is backed by rising macro indicators. GST mop-up climbed 23%, passenger car sales soared 14% to a record 525,000 units, and UPI transactions hit 25.47 billion, up 23% year-on-year. This indicates robust festive demand despite inflation and global concerns, suggesting a strong start to Q3 FY27.

articles.headline: New-Age Logistics Firms Focus on Speed for D2C Growth
articles.summary: Third-party logistics companies like Delhivery and Shadowfax are prioritising rapid delivery (same-day, next-day) as a premium service. Rising demand from D2C brands and e-commerce sellers, especially during festive seasons, drives this shift. Shadowfax's express parcels grew 55% YoY to ₹1,096 crore in Q2, commanding 15-20% higher realisations.

articles.headline: GST Revamp Gives D2C Firms Pan-India Wings
articles.summary: New GST rules, effective November 1, allow online sellers to declare e-commerce platform warehouses as their local principal place of business (PPO). This simplifies multi-state compliance, reduces costs, and streamlines nationwide logistics, benefiting 9.5 lakh small sellers ahead of Diwali and Black Friday.

articles.headline: Samsung Develops Massive 17-Inch Foldable Tablet
articles.summary: Samsung is reportedly developing a 17-inch foldable tablet that shrinks to an 8-inch form factor when folded. This project is in development across multiple versions and test devices, according to sources. Specifics beyond the screen size are not yet available.

articles.headline: Global Cloud Market Exceeds $500 Billion on AI Boom
articles.summary: Worldwide cloud infrastructure services revenues surpassed $500 billion, driven by the AI boom. Trailing twelve months as of September 30, 2026, saw revenues at $559 billion, with a YoY growth of 33%. The actual figure is likely to exceed $600 billion by year-end, highlighting strong industry expansion.

articles.headline: Sam Altman Meets Samsung Executives Amid Chip Shortages
articles.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman met Samsung Group executives in South Korea to deepen cooperation on memory chips and AI infrastructure. Discussions focused on AI's impact on industries and business. This meeting comes as global shortages in memory products intensify competition for supplies.

articles.headline: OpenAI Cuts Funding Target by $10 Billion Amid Market Shifts
articles.summary: OpenAI has cut its fundraising target by $10 billion, now seeking $20 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation. This adjustment comes due to stock selloffs and rival Anthropic's impending public listing, complicating investor commitment efforts. Some investors have reduced their commitments.

articles.headline: Micro Occasions Drive Quick Commerce and Beauty Services Boom
articles.summary: Quick commerce platforms and rapid fashion delivery apps are seeing demand spikes from "micro occasions" like Karwa Chauth and Halloween. Categories like mehendi and gift sets saw double or multiple times usual demand. Platforms are stepping up marketing with dedicated in-app pages for these impulse purchases.

articles.headline: Google Successfully Runs AI Model on Satellite in Orbit
articles.summary: Google's Project Suncatcher successfully ran an AI model on a satellite, receiving its first complete response on Earth. This marks a milestone in exploring AI computing infrastructure in space. CEO Sundar Pichai called it a "hello world" moment for the initiative.

articles.headline: DSCI Outlines Liability Framework for Autonomous AI Agents
articles.summary: The Data Security Council of India (DSCI) released an industry framework for assessing liability when autonomous AI agents cause harm. It splits responsibility across five technology layers (AI users, service providers, product companies, tool developers, infrastructure providers) based on control and decisions, rather than assigning sole liability.

articles.headline: Consent Managers Face Revenue Model Uncertainty Before Registration
articles.summary: Companies preparing to register as consent managers by November 13 are uncertain about viable revenue models. The debate continues whether data fiduciaries, technology companies, consumers, or the government should bear costs. Some expect fees from fiduciaries, while others fear large players might build in-house systems, impacting independent providers.

articles.headline: FPIs Return to Indian Stocks Amid AI Blues
articles.summary: After aggressive selling, Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) turned net buyers of Indian equities, investing nearly $1.2 billion over the past 10 trading sessions. This shift may be driven by concerns over the AI trade outlook, prompting some to reallocate to "beaten-down" Indian stocks, which have lagged global peers.

articles.headline: RBI, FIU Scrutinise Crypto Cards for Bypassing Regulations
articles.summary: RBI and the Financial Intelligence Unit are investigating the use of prepaid crypto cards by Indian residents to bypass regulations and tax scrutiny for domestic transactions. These cards, issued by overseas fintechs, convert crypto to fiat for payments, raising concerns under FEMA and potential tax evasion. Several cards have been blocked.

articles.headline: ED Files ECIR Against Subhash Chandra in LIC HFL Loan Fraud
articles.summary: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has initiated a case (ECIR) against Essel Group chairman Subhash Chandra for an alleged ₹1,322 crore loan fraud involving LIC Housing Finance. This follows a CBI FIR against Chandra and others concerning two loan facilities aggregating ₹980 crore sanctioned in 2018 to four Essel Group companies.

articles.headline: Rahul Gandhi Claims PM Modi Will Face Legal Action for "Vote Chori"
articles.summary: At the INDIA bloc rally, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi alleged PM Modi wouldn't be PM without CEC Gyanesh Kumar and "vote chori," claiming legal action would be taken against Modi and Shah. He stated 2024 Lok Sabha polls were "illegal" due to 13.5 crore deleted voters and that Kumar would go to jail.

articles.headline: BJP Counters Opposition Rally with "Save Democracy, End Anarchy" Marches
articles.summary: The BJP deployed top leaders, including party chief Nitin Nabin and Union ministers, across India in 'Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao' yatras to counter the INDIA bloc rally. BJP accused Congress of hurting Sikh sentiments by choosing November 1 for its rally and questioned attendance figures.

articles.headline: Internal Strife Plagues National Conference in J&K
articles.summary: Jammu & Kashmir's ruling National Conference faces internal strife, with ~20 MLAs seeking changes in party structure and removal of office-bearers. Dissatisfaction arose after CM Omar Abdullah's cabinet reshuffle. MLAs plan to present a memorandum to party president Farooq Abdullah, threatening further steps if concerns aren't addressed.

articles.headline: Senior BJP Leaders to Hold Padyatras in Uttar Pradesh Before Diwali
articles.summary: Senior BJP leaders, including Nitin Nabin, CM Yogi Adityanath, and Union ministers, will cover all six regions of Uttar Pradesh through padyatras as part of the 'Save Democracy, End Anarchy' campaign. The initiative aims to involve civil society and counter opposition narratives before Diwali.

articles.headline: Odisha DG Prisons Booked for Sexual Harassment
articles.summary: Odisha's DG Prisons, Susanta Kumar Nath, was booked for allegedly sexually harassing a subordinate staff member and transferred as OSD in the home department. A friend of his was also booked in the same case. The investigation is pending. Nath was an aspirant for the DGP post.

articles.headline: Minister Reviews India's First Bullet Train Manufacturing at BEML
articles.summary: Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw reviewed the manufacturing of India's first indigenous high-speed train, the Bharat Bullet Train (B-28), at BEML's Bengaluru facility. Developed for the Mumbai-Ahmedabad corridor, the project combines advanced engineering, local manufacturing, and passenger-centric design.

articles.headline: China's COVID Criticism Toughened its Global Attitude, says Foreign Secretary Misri
articles.summary: Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri stated international criticism and perceived stigmatisation over COVID-19 toughened China's attitude towards the global community. He noted Beijing's belief that it was being blamed for the pandemic, contributing to its harsh response and prolonged lockdowns. India never pointed fingers at China.

articles.headline: Karnataka Mandates State Flag Hoisting for Private Companies
articles.summary: Karnataka CM DK Shivakumar announced private companies must hoist the state's bi-colour flag, with an order expected this month. This follows renewed complaints and a pro-Kannada outfit's drive to collect data on local employment in IT/BT firms, amid concerns of bias against Kannadigas in hiring.

articles.headline: Siddaramaiah Sting Probe: Phone Changed Hands at Kumaraswamy’s Residence
articles.summary: The mobile phone used in the alleged sting targeting former Karnataka CM Siddaramaiah was purchased in Delhi and handed over at Union Minister HD Kumaraswamy's official residence. Bengaluru police cited accused Ritesh Pandey's statement, indicating the handover occurred on instructions of one Prajwal Prasad, present at the residence.

articles.headline: NEET-UG May Retain Pen & Paper Mode Due to Southern Opposition
articles.summary: The Nilekani panel's exam reform plan faces a roadblock, with southern states opposing. NEET-UG 2027 may continue in pen-and-paper alongside CBT, potentially in multiple shifts. Comprehensive reforms are now expected from 2028-29, allowing a gradual transition to familiarise students and build infrastructure for full CBT.

articles.headline: Gulf Oil Plans Return to Mexico and US, Eyes Global Listing
articles.summary: Gulf Oil Lubricants plans to re-enter Mexico in 2027 and the US via a master-licensing deal, aiming for a global listing of Gulf Oil International in 3-5 years. The company is seeking acquisitions in South America and Southeast Asia, expanding its global footprint and marine lubricants business.

articles.headline: Medicine Sales Rise in Double Digits Driven by Chronic Care
articles.summary: India's medicine sales grew in double digits for four consecutive quarters, reaching ₹70,180 crore in Q3 FY27, up 12% YoY. This surge is fueled by chronic care segments like cardiac, diabetes, and oncology. Improved diagnosis, health awareness, and a shift from smaller to larger pharma players contribute to this growth trend.

articles.headline: Gulf Investors Eye India's AI Infrastructure, Space Tech
articles.summary: Gulf-based investors are selectively exploring opportunities in India's AI infrastructure and space technology, despite subdued broader interest in Indian assets due to rupee depreciation. Data centre operator Yotta and space tech startup Pixxel are among those attracting capital, often through offshore fund vehicles.

articles.headline: Editorial: Address Local Concerns on Hydropower Projects, Not Just 'Foreign Hand'
articles.summary: The editorial argues that opposition to Siang Upper and Dibang hydropower projects stems from indigenous communities' concerns over land, livelihood, and cultural identity, not just alleged foreign funding. It highlights risks in Himalayan projects and calls for transparent answers on rehabilitation, compensation, and disaster preparedness, urging governments to address legitimate grievances.

articles.headline: Editorial: India Must Increase Gold Holdings Amid Rising G-Sec Yields
articles.summary: The editorial argues that with global financial instability and rising G-sec yields, countries, including India, have no alternative but to increase their bullion holdings. It notes the developed world's debt crisis, US treasury yield increases, and China's reduced US treasury holdings, suggesting gold as a safer reserve asset.

articles.headline: Editorial: Improve Cyclone Preparedness and Post-Storm Recovery
articles.summary: The editorial stresses the need to shorten recovery time after cyclones in India. Despite improved detection, structural engineering and environmental protection (sea walls, mangroves) are inadequate. It calls for retrofitting buildings, protecting utilities, and regular community training. Climate change impacts cyclone predictability, demanding dynamic disaster management.

articles.headline: Chartistry: AI Economy Shows New Gender Glass Ceiling
articles.summary: Women's representation in the budding AI economy is lower than in conventional jobs, creating a new glass ceiling. Senior positions in AI-related roles at AI companies have the lowest female presence: 21% at VP level and just 13% at CXO level, compared to 23% in non-AI CXO roles.

articles.headline: Opinion: Embrace Technological Fasting for Well-being
articles.summary: The opinion piece advocates for "technological fasting" to counter the frantic pace of modern life and over-reliance on mobile devices. It suggests limiting screen time, observing nightly digital detox, and replacing digital consumption with traditional activities like reading, gardening, or playing music to improve mental health and foster creativity.

articles.headline: Chartistry: West Asia Remains Top Foreign Destination for Indian Travellers
articles.summary: West Asia remains the prime hotspot for Indian outbound travellers, with nearly 50% heading to the region. The UAE accounts for 27.7% of trips, and Saudi Arabia 12.1%. This trend continues despite global concerns, indicating strong regional connectivity and preference.

articles.headline: Ferrari CEO Discusses Innovation, India, and Powertrains
articles.summary: Ferrari CEO Benedetto Vigna discusses the future of electric cars, the economics of scarcity and exclusivity, and Ferrari's growing ambitions in India. He touches on balancing heritage with innovation and his philosophy on leadership and risk-taking.

articles.headline: Electric Car Sales Double in India Amid Rising Fuel Prices
articles.summary: Electric car sales in India nearly doubled to 35,777 units in October, making up 7% of total passenger vehicle sales. High fuel prices, improved charging infrastructure, and new model launches propelled this shift. Tata Motors led the EV market with 40.7% share, followed by Mahindra (23.7%).

articles.headline: Irdai to Evaluate Feedback on Proposed Insurance Selling Fee Overhaul
articles.summary: The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (Irdai) will evaluate stakeholder feedback on its proposed overhaul of insurance commissions and distribution expenses. The plan, which aims to curb distribution costs and improve transparency, could reduce broker revenue by up to 60%, raising industry concerns.

articles.headline: BYD Reports 11% Sales Rise in October Driven by Strong Exports
articles.summary: Chinese EV maker BYD posted an 11% sales growth in October, reaching 490,168 units, with overseas shipments soaring 102.8% to 170,194 units. This marks its sixth straight month of sales growth, relying on international markets to counter sluggish domestic demand and intense price competition.

articles.headline: Xiaomi's October EV Deliveries Surpass 50,000 Units
articles.summary: Chinese smartphone maker Xiaomi announced its electric vehicle deliveries exceeded 50,000 units in October, marking its highest monthly total this year. This ramps up production to meet its 2026 target, following 30,000 units in August and 40,000 in September, with 336,000 vehicles delivered year-to-date.

articles.headline: Reliance Retail Expects Margin Growth from Next Fiscal Year
articles.summary: Reliance Retail expects its operating EBITDA margins to grow from next fiscal year as investments in e-commerce and quick commerce begin to pay off. The retailer is ramping up dark stores and remodelling existing ones for rapid deliveries, expecting to leverage its asset base for significant growth.

articles.headline: McDonald’s India to Invest $80 Million in North & East Expansion
articles.summary: McDonald’s India (North & East) will invest $80 million over the next 2.5 years for store expansion and digitisation to boost consumer demand and compete with rivals. This is its highest two-year investment, funded internally, though profitability may remain pressured by rising food, packaging, and transport inflation.

articles.headline: Fairfax-Backed Maxop Engineering Acquires Majority Stake in Faith Automation
articles.summary: Fairfax-backed Maxop Engineering has acquired a majority stake in Pune-based Faith Automation Systems and Tooling. The design and engineering firm automates production lines for auto manufacturers like Maruti Suzuki, Toyota, and Tata Motors. Industry experts estimate the deal's enterprise value at ₹400-500 crore.

articles.headline: AB InBev Sets Aside $30 Million for Unpaid Dues in Telangana
articles.summary: Anheuser-Busch InBev, the world's largest brewer, has provisioned $30 million for outstanding payments from the Telangana government. This highlights financial risks in India's state-controlled alcohol markets, where delayed payments and price restrictions squeeze brewers. The state allegedly owes alcohol companies nearly $400 million in total dues.

articles.headline: Liquor Market Growth Slows as Mass-Market Segment Suffers
articles.summary: India’s spirits market volume growth slowed to 4.6% YoY in Q3 FY27 from 6.4%, primarily due to weakness in the mass-market segment. Inflatiory pressures, prolonged West Asia crisis, and softer monsoons are squeezing lower-income consumers, impacting sales for brands like Officer's Choice. Prestige segment grew 5.7%.

articles.headline: PM Modi to Meet Niti Aayog Leadership to Shape FY28 Budget
articles.summary: PM Narendra Modi will meet Niti Aayog's new leadership on Nov 5 to hear sectoral priorities for the 2027-28 budget. Discussions will focus on long-term development goals for "Viksit Bharat by 2047," reviewing the Aayog's work and identifying opportunities amid global uncertainty.

articles.headline: State-Run General Insurers to Submit Turnaround Plans
articles.summary: State-run general insurers will submit board-approved plans to scale back or exit unprofitable segments, as mounting losses pressure an overhaul. New India Assurance reported a ₹1,267 crore Q2 FY27 loss. A parliamentary committee recommended a time-bound roadmap for organic solvency and improved claim ratio.

articles.headline: Solar Module Manufacturers Seek Extension for Local Sourcing Compliance
articles.summary: Solar module manufacturers are requesting an extension for the deadline to comply with compulsory local sourcing of cells beyond January. They highlight a significant gap between domestic module capacity (160 GW) and compliant cell supply (15.8 GW), arguing that non-integrated makers bear higher costs due to this imbalance.

articles.headline: CII Urges GST-Like Reforms in Land, Labour, Local Approvals
articles.summary: CII recommends extending GST Council's decriminalisation approach to land, labour, construction, and local approvals. This aims to reduce compliance costs, accelerate investments, and foster trust-based governance by simplifying regulations, streamlining permits, and tackling overlapping requirements across states.

articles.headline: Three South Korean Auto Suppliers to Invest ₹1,614 Crore in Andhra
articles.summary: Three South Korean automotive component manufacturers—Hwashin, Seoyon, and Iwamet—will invest ₹1,614 crore in Anantapur, Andhra Pradesh, creating 1,418 jobs. This follows an AP delegation's visit to South Korea, marking a win for AP and a setback for Tamil Nadu, which had also courted these suppliers.

articles.headline: FPIs Inject $1.2 Billion into D-Street Amid AI Sell-Off Concerns
articles.summary: Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) turned net buyers of Indian equities, investing nearly $1.2 billion in 10 sessions. This "anti-AI trade" shift suggests money moving from overvalued AI stocks to "beaten-down" Indian large-caps. However, some analysts caution these are positional flows, not a broad bullish call on India.

articles.headline: Unseasonal Headwinds May Dampen November Equity Market Performance
articles.summary: Investors face a challenging November despite historical seasonality favouring Indian equities. Elevated crude oil prices (near $115/barrel), rising global bond yields, and a weak rupee present headwinds. While festive activity extends and FPIs return, experts caution crude oil remains a key risk.

articles.headline: Julius Baer CEO Warns of AI Bubble, Sees India Growth Intact
articles.summary: Julius Baer CEO Stefan Bollinger warns of an "AI bubble" as the biggest global market risk. On India, he considers the correction in equity valuations (from 21-22x to 16-16.5x earnings) healthy and views India's growth story as intact. He also notes increasing diversification by wealthy Indians into offshore investments.

articles.headline: Foreign G-Sec Selling Halves, But Risks Persist for Inflows
articles.summary: Foreign selling of Indian government securities nearly halved in October, offering respite after outflows. However, high oil prices, elevated global yields, and AI investment uncertainty cloud sustained revival prospects. FPIs sold ₹5,400 crore of G-secs, down from ₹46,390 crore in September.

articles.headline: Mutual Funds Consistently Add Six Stocks Amid Market Slump
articles.summary: Despite a prolonged market slump, mutual fund managers are finding investment opportunities. Six BSE 500 stocks saw consistent rise in mutual fund holding for four quarters since Sept 2025, with MFs holding at least 10% of share capital and average RoE > 15%.

articles.headline: RIL's Q2 Earnings Boosted by O2C, Digital, Despite Retail Pressures
articles.summary: Reliance Industries (RIL) reported strong Q2 FY27 revenue (₹3.6 lakh crore, up 27.8% YoY) and profit growth, led by oil-to-chemicals (O2C) with Ebitda up 67.9%. Digital platforms saw double-digit growth. Retail Ebitda declined 10.2% due to digital commerce investments, festive calendar shift, and rising inflation/rupee depreciation.

articles.headline: Sun Pharma's Q2 Revenue Boosted by India, Specialty Medicines
articles.summary: Sun Pharmaceutical reported strong double-digit revenue growth in Q2 FY27, driven by robust performance in India, emerging markets, and specialty medicines (Ilumya, Unloxcyt, Leqselvi). Profitability was impacted by one-off acquisition/litigation costs. R&D investments expected to increase in H2 FY27.

articles.headline: Insurers Worry as Cyberattacks on Financial Institutions Rise
articles.summary: Insurers are concerned about rising cyberattacks on financial institutions and manufacturing companies, fearing significant losses from data exposure. Recent breaches at SBI, BoB, and AU SFB highlight growing vulnerabilities. Insurers anticipate higher premiums as the threat landscape, involving AI-powered hacks, becomes more complex.

articles.headline: Nifty Faces Key 23,200 Hurdle for Near-Term Rebound
articles.summary: Nifty rose nearly 2% last week to close around 23,050, but analysts are cautious as it approaches the 23,200 resistance. A breakout could lead to 23,500-23,600, with support at 22,600-22,800. Technical indicators suggest continued weakness if it fails to breach the hurdle.

articles.headline: Banks Leverage AI to Boost Productivity, Reduce Costs by Up to 50%
articles.summary: Indian banks report 10-50% productivity improvements from AI initiatives in corporate banking, collections, and transaction processing. Kotak Mahindra Bank saw massive efficiency gains from AI in wholesale banking, enabling staff to handle 20-30% more volumes. HDFC Bank reduced service delivery times by 30% through digitisation.

articles.headline: Harry Kane Misses Penalty After Winning Ballon d’Or
articles.summary: Harry Kane missed a penalty in his first game for Bayern Munich after winning the Ballon d’Or. He hit the crossbar against Dortmund, resulting in a 2-2 draw. Kane, however, contributed to Bayern's second goal. He became the first Bayern player in 45 years to win the award.

articles.headline: Kylian Mbappe Scores Penalty in Real Win Amid Controversy
articles.summary: Kylian Mbappe scored a penalty, helping Real Madrid win 3-0 against Racing Santander. This comes after a tumultuous week where he lost the Ballon d'Or and apologised for a social media joke about former Chinese leader Mao Zedong, leading to brand partnership terminations.

articles.headline: LeBron James Shines in Philadelphia 76ers Win at 41
articles.summary: LeBron James, approaching 42, delivered a vintage performance for the NBA champion 76ers, closing out a 98-93 win with a go-ahead bucket and nearly achieving a triple-double (9 rebounds, 8 assists). He emphasized his continued passion and competitive spirit, enjoying his record 24th NBA season.

articles.headline: Mumbai Property Registrations Remain Strong in October
articles.summary: Mumbai recorded its second-highest October property registrations with 12,690 transactions, up 9% YoY, despite the Shraddh period and fewer Navratri registration days. Stamp duty collections rose 13% to ₹1,173 crore. This indicates resilient housing demand heading into the peak festive season.

articles.headline: NCRTC Eyes Realty Hubs Along Namo Bharat Corridor
articles.summary: The National Capital Region Transport Corporation (NCRTC) plans to develop real estate hubs along the Delhi-Ghaziabad-Meerut Namo Bharat corridor and other proposed lines. It aims to leverage regional connectivity for mixed-use, transit-oriented development (TOD) to attract private investment in commercial, residential, and institutional projects.

articles.headline: House Panel to Review Media Law Implementation, Regulatory Overlaps
articles.summary: A parliamentary standing committee will review the implementation of media laws, focusing on OTT platforms, social media, TRPs, and Pay-TV. The review addresses convergence of broadcast and digital platforms, regulatory overlaps, accountability, and the need for a comprehensive Media Bill, having received inputs from MeitY.

articles.headline: Sebi to Delist Inactive Companies, Tighten Penny Stock Oversight
articles.summary: Sebi will delist companies with no economic activity from stock exchanges to protect investors, especially those in penny stocks. Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey stated such firms pose manipulation risks. Sebi also plans an AI-based system to monitor inactive companies and will issue a consultation paper on FII compliance.

articles.headline: Banks Seek Extension of Micro Loan Credit Guarantee Fund
articles.summary: Banks have asked the government to extend the Credit Guarantee Fund for Micro Units (CGFMU) program, which ended March 31, 2026. Lenders fear higher provisioning and risk costs for unsecured micro loans if the scheme isn't reopened soon, impacting asset quality and access to credit for bottom-of-the-pyramid borrowers.

articles.headline: Trump White House Prepares for Democratic Congressional Takeover
articles.summary: President Donald Trump's White House is preparing for a possible Democratic takeover of Congress by developing plans to advance his agenda through executive orders and bracing for investigations. Senior officials are identifying executive actions on immigration, tariffs, housing, and federal spending, while Trump threatens vetoes.

articles.headline: AIramco Acquires 49% Stake in Saudi AI Company Humain
articles.summary: Saudi oil major Aramco is acquiring a 49% stake in state-backed AI company Humain, injecting cash and assets. The Public Investment Fund retains 51%. This aims to accelerate Humain's global growth and AI capabilities, with plans to deploy three gigawatts of AI data center capacity by 2030.

articles.headline: Bolsonaro Can Stay in US Indefinitely, Says Trump
articles.summary: Former US President Donald Trump said defeated Brazilian presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro can stay in the United States indefinitely. Trump claimed the Brazilian election was "a disgrace." Bolsonaro left Brazil after losing to Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva.

articles.headline: Prediction Market Bettors Seek Midterm Edge in US
articles.summary: A small group of prediction market traders conducted field trips to Maine and Los Angeles, then analysed polls and voter data from Brazil, Israel, and Texas, to gain an edge in wagering on US midterm election outcomes. This legwork has paid off, with some traders making significant profits.

articles.headline: Gen Z Protests Erupt in Germany Demanding Education, Health Reforms
articles.summary: A group named "Gen Z regelt" called for demonstrations across Germany demanding reforms in education, health, climate protection, and affordable living. The mass protests escalated into violence in cities like Frankfurt, Cologne, Hamburg, and Berlin, as rioters confronted police.

articles.headline: Mahadev Betting Kingpin Extradited from Oman by CBI
articles.summary: CBI, with UAE authorities & Interpol, extradited Saurabh Chandrakar, alleged mastermind of the ₹6,000-crore Mahadev online gambling syndicate, from Oman to India. He faces a Raipur special CBI court for money laundering and illegal betting. The syndicate paid public servants and used international "panels" and mule accounts for bets on sports. He's wanted in two CBI cases and an ED case.

articles.headline: DigiYatra International Trials Begin at Seven Indian Airports
articles.summary: DigiYatra's biometric facial recognition trials for international passengers began at seven Indian airports (Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Cochin, Chennai, Amritsar). Eligible e-passport holders on select Air India/IndiGo flights can use it at touchpoints, aiming for seamless travel and reduced processing times. A wider rollout is planned by 2027.

articles.headline: Sindhu, Sen Clinch Hylo Open Titles in Germany
articles.summary: Indian shuttlers PV Sindhu and Lakshya Sen secured a rare double victory at the Hylo Open Super 500 in Saarbrucken, Germany. Sindhu defeated Line Højmark Kjaersfeldt 21-12, 21-14, ending her title drought since 2022. Sen triumphed over Jonatan Christie 21-17, 21-10, marking his first title of 2026 and boosting rankings.

articles.headline: Indian PV Sales Hit Record 5.3 Lakh Units in October
articles.summary: Indian passenger vehicle wholesale sales hit a record 5.25-5.3 lakh units in October, driven by strong festive demand (Dhanteras/Diwali). Maruti Suzuki (2.12 lakh units, +20.5%), Hyundai, Mahindra, Tata (21% jump), and Kia reported record monthly sales, contributing to 13-15% YoY growth. EV registrations also hit 3.5 lakh units, and two-wheelers surged 50% YoY, though high dealer inventory is a concern.

articles.headline: India Wins T20I Series 3-2 Despite Final Match Loss
articles.summary: India secured the five-match T20I series against New Zealand 3-2, despite losing the final match in Hamilton by 7 wickets. NZ chased India's 191/8 in 18.2 overs, led by Tim Seifert's 93 and Glenn Phillips' 65. Ishan Kishan (61) and Shreyas Iyer (50) scored for India. This marks India's first series win in NZ since 2020-21.

articles.headline: Jharkhand Police Station Staff Shunted After Alleged Rape
articles.summary: All personnel at Gamharia police station, Seraikela-Kharsawan, including the officer-in-charge, were suspended or transferred following the alleged rape of a woman inside the station on October 29. A Sub-Inspector, constable, and another person were arrested, bringing total arrests to three. A special investigation team was formed to probe the incident.

articles.headline: RBI Approves Record ₹2.11 Lakh Crore Dividend to Government
articles.summary: The RBI board approved a record ₹2.11 lakh crore surplus transfer to the government for FY24, more than double the previous year's and exceeding estimates. This payout, attributed to higher interest income from foreign assets and liquidity operations, is expected to help achieve fiscal deficit targets and boost infrastructure capital expenditure.

articles.headline: SEBI Proposes Strict Regulations for Financial Influencers
articles.summary: SEBI proposed a new regulatory framework for 'finfluencers' to curb unauthorized investment advice. Influencers must register with SEBI and disclose financial product affiliations. Regulated entities are prohibited from associating with unregistered individuals offering specific investment recommendations. The move aims to protect retail investors from misleading social media and market manipulation.

articles.headline: DeepSeek Releases Autonomous 'Super-agent' Coding AI in Beta
articles.summary: DeepSeek released 'Super-agent', an open-source autonomous coding AI prototype, to rival Anthropic's Claude Code. This beta offering proactively monitors developer chats for coding issues and suggests solutions without explicit summoning, aiming to minimize human attention while maximizing value in software development.

articles.headline: IAF Chief Prioritizes Indigenous Fighters, Combat Strength
articles.summary: India's 29th Chief of Air Staff, Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, outlined his "VAYU" agenda, prioritizing indigenous Tejas Mark-1A, Mk2, and AMCA fighters, along with Indian sensors and weapons. His foremost task is restoring IAF's combat strength to sanctioned levels, aiming for deterrence by fighting with Indian solutions and holding them in numbers.

articles.headline: OPEC+ Holds December Crude Oil Output Targets Steady
articles.summary: OPEC+ oil-producing countries maintained December crude oil production targets steady, as policy adjustments are anticipated next year. The 21-country bloc continues to grapple with export disruptions from the Iran war, which has led to elevated crude oil prices. Members will meet on November 29 to decide 2027 quotas.

articles.headline: Binance Resumes Withdrawals After Covering 95% of $6.3B Heist
articles.summary: Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange, resumed withdrawals for Bitcoin and 15 major assets after covering 95% ($6 billion) of the $6.3 billion stolen in the largest digital heist. The FBI attributed the attack to North Korea's TraderTraitor unit, which allegedly converted stolen assets to Ether. Binance used its own funds, planning to cover the remaining 5% of less liquid assets in phases.

articles.headline: Iranian Negotiators in Doha for Third Day of Peace Talks
articles.summary: Iranian negotiators are in Doha for a third day of talks with Qatari mediators, aiming for a deal to end the US-Israeli war on Iran, amid concerns of conflict escalation post-US midterms. Iran's Supreme Leader ordered forces to prepare for attacks. While Trump mentioned productive talks, he hasn't ruled out further military action.

articles.headline: Judge Dismisses Trump's $10 Billion Defamation Suit Against WSJ
articles.summary: A federal judge in Miami dismissed Donald Trump's $10 billion defamation lawsuit against The Wall Street Journal and Rupert Murdoch "with prejudice," meaning it cannot be refiled. Trump failed to prove actual malice in the article, which concerned his alleged ties to Jeffrey Epstein and a suggestive birthday letter.

articles.headline: Bangladesh Forms Wage Board Amid Violent Garment Protests
articles.summary: Bangladesh formed a six-member wage board to review garment workers' pay following violent protests demanding higher wages. Workers are seeking a monthly minimum of 30,000 taka ($245), more than double the current 12,500 taka, citing rising living costs. The protests disrupted transport and factory operations in industrial areas.

articles.headline: Commercial LPG, Jet Fuel Prices Hike Third Consecutive Month
articles.summary: Oil companies increased commercial LPG cylinder prices by ₹10 (19-kg now ₹2,820 in Delhi) and 5-kg refills by ₹2.5. Aviation Turbine Fuel (ATF) rates also rose by ₹1.37/litre to ₹138.5 in Delhi. This marks the third consecutive monthly hike for both, impacting hotels, restaurants, and airlines, driven by rising projected under-recoveries. Domestic LPG prices remained unchanged.

articles.headline: First Vande Bharat Sleeper Express Flagged Off, Exports Planned
articles.summary: Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw flagged off South India's first Vande Bharat Sleeper Express connecting Bengaluru and Mumbai (16 hours). The 16-coach train features 823 berths and improved amenities. Commercial services begin Tuesday. The Minister also announced plans to export Vande Bharat trains within 3-4 years and that the design for India's B-28 indigenous bullet train is ready for a 2027 rollout.

articles.headline: Char Dham Helicopter Operators Threaten Halt Over Two-Pilot Rule
articles.summary: Following a fatal Badrinath crash on October 30, DGCA mandated two pilots for all Char Dham helicopter flights, effective November 2, requiring hilly terrain-qualified co-pilots and clearances. Eleven operators threaten to suspend services from Monday, arguing the rule is commercially unviable due to increased costs and logistics, and are seeking an urgent review.

articles.headline: Four Die Cleaning Hotel Waste Chamber in Ujjain
articles.summary: Four people, including a hotel supervisor and three sanitation workers, died while cleaning an underground waste chamber at a Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh hotel. They were trapped by muck and suspected poisonous gas after one fell and others attempted rescue without protective gear. All were declared dead at the hospital. CM Mohan Yadav announced ₹4 lakh aid per family.

articles.headline: Two AAP MLAs, Including Ex-Minister, Quit Ahead of Punjab Polls
articles.summary: Two AAP MLAs, including former minister Chetan Singh Jouramajra (dropped from cabinet in 2024) and Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra, resigned from the party's primary membership in Punjab, ahead of the 2027 assembly elections. They cited the government's failure to control the drug menace and fulfill 2022 promises, with speculation they may join the BJP.

articles.headline: Harmanpreet's Hat-Trick Leads India to Victory Over Malaysia
articles.summary: Captain Harmanpreet Singh's hat-trick led the Indian hockey team to a 4-2 victory over Malaysia in a closely fought Asian Champions Trophy match in Jalandhar. Sukhjeet Singh added another goal, securing India's undefeated status in the league stage and confirming their place in the semifinals alongside Japan and Korea. Harmanpreet converted two penalty corners and a penalty stroke.

articles.headline: Karnataka Minister Denies Honda Is Exiting the State
articles.summary: Karnataka Industries Minister MB Patil dismissed Union Minister HD Kumaraswamy's "baseless" claims that Honda Motorcycle and Scooter India is exiting the state. Patil stated Honda has manufactured in Kolar since 2011, employs over 7,800, operates its second-largest plant there, and plans EV two-wheeler production. He confirmed no government lapses or company dissatisfaction.

articles.headline: Delhi Curbs: 714 Non-BS-VI Vehicles Turned Away on Day 1
articles.summary: Delhi implemented a ban on non-BS-VI vehicles registered outside the city as part of winter air pollution curbs, effective until January 31. On day one, 714 vehicles were turned away and 38 overage vehicles impounded. The enforcement caused long traffic jams at border checkpoints, especially on Delhi-Gurugram routes.

articles.headline: Indian Auto Sales, EV Two-Wheelers Hit Record Highs in October
articles.summary: India's auto sales and EV two-wheeler sales reached record highs in October, driven by festive demand. Car sales rose 13-14% YoY to 5.25-5.3 lakh units, with Maruti, Mahindra, Hyundai, and Kia reporting record monthly figures. Electric two-wheeler sales surged 48% YoY to 2.24 lakh units, led by TVS Motor (27% share), Bajaj Auto (21.92%), and Ather Energy (14.20%).
